confidenceNote.zh: 190年後朝廷號令不出都門，疆界僅具名義。
confidenceNote.en: After 190 the court's writ barely ran; the extent shown is nominal.

summary.zh: 東漢末年，宦官外戚交爭，黃巾亂後州牧擁兵割據，漢室名存實亡，終於建安二十五年禪位於魏。
summary.en: The Eastern Han in its last decades: after the Yellow Turban rising, provincial governors ruled in all but name, and in 220 the last emperor abdicated to Wei.

summary.zh: 曹丕受漢禪所建，都洛陽，據中原與河北，三國中最強。甘露之後政歸司馬氏，咸熙二年禪於晉。
summary.en: Founded when Cao Pi accepted the Han abdication in 220. Based at Luoyang, it held the northern heartland — the strongest of the three — until the Sima clan took power from within and replaced it with Jin in 266.

summary.zh: 劉備於成都稱帝，自承漢統。諸葛亮輔政，南撫夷越，北伐中原；景元四年魏滅之。
summary.en: Liu Bei proclaimed himself emperor at Chengdu in 221 as the continuation of the Han. Under Zhuge Liang it pacified the southwest and campaigned north against Wei; it fell to Wei in 263.

summary.zh: 孫氏三世據江東。孫權黃武元年建元，黃龍元年稱帝，都建業。恃長江之險，立國最久，至太康元年降晉。
summary.en: The Sun family's state on the lower Yangtze. Sun Quan took imperial title in 229 with his capital at Jianye. Shielded by the river, it outlasted the others, surrendering to Jin in 280.

summary.zh: 司馬炎受魏禪建晉，都洛陽。太康元年滅吳，三國歸一。惠帝時八王之亂，永嘉五年（311）洛陽陷落，建興四年（316）長安陷落，愍帝出降，西晉亡；次年司馬睿於建康稱晉王，是為東晉。
summary.en: Founded in 266 when Sima Yan accepted the Wei abdication. In 280 it conquered Wu and reunified the empire. Under Emperor Hui the War of the Eight Princes broke the state; Luoyang fell in 311 and Chang'an in 316, when Emperor Min surrendered and the Western Jin ended. The next year Sima Rui took the title King of Jin at Jiankang: the Eastern Jin.

summary.zh: 東漢末政治家、軍事家、詩人。迎獻帝都許，挾天子以令諸侯；破袁紹於官渡，統一北方；赤壁受挫，三分之勢遂成。封魏王，其子丕代漢。
summary.en: Statesman, general and poet of the late Han. He took the emperor under his control at Xu, crushed Yuan Shao at Guandu and unified the north; checked at Red Cliffs, he consolidated a state his son would turn into the Wei dynasty.

label.en: Raises troops at Chenliu against Dong Zhuo
Defeated at Red Cliffs; withdraws north
Defeats Ma Chao and Han Sui at Tong Pass
Created King of Wei at Ye

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 庚子，王崩于洛陽，年六十六。
passages.textEn: On the day gengzi, the King died at Luoyang, aged sixty-six.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Pei Songzhi's commentary quoting the Weiwu gushi
passages.locator: 卷一 裴註引《魏武故事》載〈讓縣自明本志令〉
passages.textZh: 設使國家無有孤，不知當幾人稱帝，幾人稱王。
passages.textEn: Had the state been without me, I know not how many would have styled themselves emperor, and how many king.

summary.zh: 涿郡人，自稱中山靖王之後。半生流離，赤壁後據荊南，西取益州，章武元年稱帝於成都，續漢正統；夷陵敗後崩於白帝城。
summary.en: A claimed descendant of the Han royal house who spent decades as a wandering warlord. After Red Cliffs he took southern Jing and then Yi Province, proclaiming himself Han emperor at Chengdu in 221; he died at Baidicheng after the Yiling defeat.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 夏四月癸巳，先主殂於永安宮，時年六十三。
passages.textEn: In the fourth month, on the day guisi, the First Sovereign died in the Yong'an Palace, aged sixty-three.

fiction.zh: 桃園三結義為小說情節。《關羽傳》只說先主與關、張「寢則同床，恩若兄弟」。
fiction.en: The Peach Garden oath is the novel's. The history says only that Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei "shared a bed, with the affection of brothers".

summary.zh: 繼父兄之業據江東。赤壁決策抗曹，奠定三分；黃龍元年稱帝，都建業。
summary.en: Inherited the Sun family's hold on the lower Yangtze at eighteen. His decision to resist Cao Cao at Red Cliffs fixed the tripartite division; he took imperial title in 229 at Jianye.

summary.zh: 蜀漢丞相。隆中對策，定下聯吳拒曹、跨有荊益之計；輔後主，建興三年南征，六年起五次北伐（六年春出祁山，同年冬圍陳倉，七年取武都、陰平，九年再出祁山，十二年出斜谷），十二年八月卒於五丈原軍中，年五十四。
summary.en: Chancellor of Shu Han. His Longzhong plan set the strategy of alliance with Wu and a base in Jing and Yi. As regent he campaigned in the south in 225 and from 228 led five northern expeditions (Qishan in spring 228, Chencang that winter, Wudu and Yinping in 229, Qishan again in 231, the Xie Valley in 234), dying in camp at the Wuzhang Plains in the eighth month of 234, aged fifty-four by Chinese reckoning.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十五 蜀書 諸葛亮傳
passages.textZh: 相持百餘日。其年八月，亮疾病，卒于軍，時年五十四。
passages.textEn: They faced each other for over a hundred days. In the eighth month of that year Liang fell ill and died in camp, aged fifty-four.

fiction.zh: 「六出祁山」、草船借箭、借東風、空城計，皆非史實。五次北伐中出祁山的只有兩次；「空城計」出自郭沖之說，裴松之已駁其不實（當時司馬懿尚在荊州）；「七擒孟獲」見於裴註所引《漢晉春秋》，陳壽本文不載。
fiction.en: "Six campaigns from Qishan", the straw boats, the east wind and the empty-fort ruse are not history. Only two of the five expeditions went by Qishan. The empty-fort story comes from Guo Chong and was refuted by Pei Songzhi (Sima Yi was then still in Jing province). The "seven captures of Meng Huo" appear in the Han Jin chunqiu quoted by Pei, not in Chen Shou's text.

summary.zh: 廬江舒人，佐孫策、孫權定江東。赤壁之戰為聯軍主帥，縱火破曹；謀取益州未行，病卒於巴丘，年三十六。
summary.en: The Sun family's leading commander. At Red Cliffs he led the allied fleet and broke Cao Cao's armada by fire; planning a drive into Yi Province, he fell ill and died at Baqiu aged thirty-six.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 吳書 周瑜傳
passages.textZh: 瑜還江陵為行裝，而道於巴丘病卒，時年三十六。
passages.textEn: Yu returned to Jiangling to make ready, but on the road he fell ill and died at Baqiu, aged thirty-six.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 吳書 周瑜傳
passages.textZh: 性度恢廓，大率為得人，惟與程普不睦。
passages.textEn: He was generous and broad-minded and on the whole won people over; only with Cheng Pu was he on bad terms.

fiction.zh: 諸葛亮「三氣周瑜」、「既生瑜，何生亮」皆出小說。史稱周瑜「性度恢廓，大率為得人」。
fiction.en: Zhuge Liang "thrice enraging Zhou Yu" and the cry "since Yu was born, why Liang?" are the novel's. The history describes Zhou Yu as generous and broad-minded, a man who won people over.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年無確載。
confidenceNote.en: Birth year not reliably recorded.

summary.zh: 出身四世三公之家，討董卓盟主，據河北四州，為北方最強；官渡敗後病卒。
summary.en: Scion of the grandest official family of the age and leader of the coalition against Dong Zhuo, he held four northern provinces — the strongest warlord of the 190s — until Guandu broke him.

note.en: Wei restored the water radical in 220

summary.zh: 東漢都城。初平元年董卓焚毀，遷帝西去；後為曹魏、西晉都。311年為漢趙所陷；北魏孝文帝494年遷都於此，534年東魏遷鄴後殘破，楊衒之547年重遊，作《洛陽伽藍記》。
summary.en: Capital of the Eastern Han, burned by Dong Zhuo in 190 when he dragged the court west; rebuilt to serve as the capital of Wei and then Western Jin. Taken by Han-Zhao in 311; Emperor Xiaowen of Wei moved his capital here in 494; after the Eastern Wei court left for Ye in 534 it fell to ruin, which Yang Xuanzhi described on revisiting it in 547.

passages.sourceEn: Record of the Buddhist Monasteries of Luoyang (Yang Xuanzhi, 547)
passages.textZh: 至武定五年，歲在丁卯，余因行役，重覽洛陽。城郭崩毀，宮室傾覆，寺觀灰燼，廟塔丘墟。牆被蒿艾，巷羅荊棘，野獸穴於荒階，山鳥巢於庭樹。
passages.textEn: In the fifth year of Wuding, the year dingmao [547], my duties took me to see Luoyang again. The walls had crumbled, the palaces fallen, the monasteries were ash and the temples and pagodas mounds of rubble. Wormwood covered the walls and brambles filled the lanes; wild beasts made their dens in the abandoned stairways and mountain birds nested in the courtyard trees.

summary.zh: 西漢故都。初平元年董卓挾獻帝西遷於此。其後為前趙、前秦、後秦、西魏、北周及隋之都。
summary.en: The old Western Han capital, to which Dong Zhuo dragged Emperor Xian in 190. Later the capital of Former Zhao, Former Qin, Later Qin, Western Wei, Northern Zhou and Sui.

summary.zh: 建安元年曹操迎獻帝都許，漢末朝廷所在。
summary.en: Cao Cao installed Emperor Xian here in 196; the nominal Han court sat here until 220.

summary.zh: 袁紹舊治；建安九年曹操克之，營為霸府，魏王國都於此。後為後趙、前燕、東魏、北齊之都。580年尉遲迥起兵失敗後，楊堅焚毀鄴城。
summary.en: Yuan Shao's seat, taken by Cao Cao in 204 and built into his power base; capital of his Kingdom of Wei from 213. Later the capital of Later Zhao, Former Yan, Eastern Wei and Northern Qi. After Yuchi Jiong's rising failed in 580, Yang Jian had Ye burned.

summary.zh: 益州治所，天府之國。章武元年劉備即帝位於此，為蜀漢都。後為成漢都城（304–347）；553年西魏取之。
summary.en: Seat of Yi Province in the rich Sichuan basin; Liu Bei took the imperial title here in 221, making it the Shu Han capital. Later the capital of Cheng-Han (304–347); Western Wei took it in 553.

note.en: renamed 313; capital of the Southern Dynasties

summary.zh: 本名秣陵；孫權徙治改名建業，黃龍元年定為吳都。即今南京，六朝金粉自此始。東晉及宋、齊、梁、陳皆都於此，合吳稱六朝。589年隋軍入城，陳亡。
summary.en: Originally Moling; Sun Quan moved his seat here in 211 and renamed it Jianye, making it the Wu capital from 229. As Jiankang it later anchored the Southern Dynasties — modern Nanjing. Eastern Jin, Song, Qi, Liang and Chen all made it their capital — with Wu, the "Six Dynasties". Sui troops entered it in 589 and Chen fell.

summary.zh: 秦嶺巴山間的戰略盆地，蜀魏必爭之地。曹操建安二十年取之，二十四年劉備奪之，為蜀漢北門。
summary.en: The strategic basin between the Qinling and Ba ranges — Cao Cao took it in 215, Liu Bei wrested it away in 219, and it remained Shu's northern gate.

summary.zh: 荊州重鎮，控扼長江中游。赤壁戰前曹操屯軍於此。552年梁元帝即位於此；554年西魏攻破，元帝被殺，其後為附庸西魏、北周的後梁所都（555–587）。
summary.en: The stronghold of Jing Province on the middle Yangtze; Cao Cao's staging base before Red Cliffs. Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne here in 552; Western Wei sacked it in 554 and killed him, and it then served as capital of the Later Liang, a client of Western Wei and Northern Zhou (555–587).

label.en: capital of Liang under Emperor Yuan

summary.zh: 劉表治所，荊州北門，南北交通咽喉。東晉孝武帝時於此僑立雍州，宋元嘉二十六年（449）立為實土。501年蕭衍自此起兵。
summary.en: Liu Biao's seat and the northern gateway of Jing Province. Under Emperor Xiaowu of Eastern Jin an émigré Yong Province was set up here, made a real province by Song in 449. Xiao Yan rose here in 501.

passages.locator: 卷三十七 州郡志三 雍州
passages.textZh: 雍州刺史，晉江左立。胡亡氐亂，雍、秦流民多南出樊、沔，晉孝武始於襄陽僑立雍州，并立僑郡縣。
passages.textEn: Yong Province was set up by Jin south of the Yangtze. When the Hu [Later Zhao] fell and the Di [Former Qin] were in turmoil, refugees from Yong and Qin came south in numbers to the Fan and Mian rivers, and Emperor Xiaowu of Jin first set up an émigré Yong Province at Xiangyang, with émigré commanderies and counties.

summary.zh: 魏東南要塞，孫吳屢攻不克，張遼威震逍遙津即在此。
summary.en: Wei's southeastern fortress, besieged again and again by Wu — the scene of Zhang Liao's famous stand in 215.

confidenceNote.zh: 確址不明：有蒲圻（今赤壁市）、嘉魚、黃州等說，本圖暫取蒲圻說並標示不確定範圍。
confidenceNote.en: The site is not established: Puqi (modern Chibi City), Jiayu and Huangzhou have all been proposed. Shown provisionally at Puqi with an uncertainty halo.

summary.zh: 長江南岸赤色崖壁，建安十三年冬孫劉聯軍破曹之地。
summary.en: The red river cliffs on the south bank of the Yangtze where the allied fleet broke Cao Cao in the winter of 208.

summary.zh: 沛國譙縣，曹氏故里。
summary.en: Qiao county in Pei — the Cao family's home.

summary.zh: 瞿塘峽口要塞。夷陵敗後劉備退守於此，章武三年託孤諸葛亮，崩於永安宮。
summary.en: The fortress at the mouth of the Qutang Gorge. Liu Bei fell back here after Yiling and died in 223, entrusting his heir to Zhuge Liang.

confidenceNote.zh: 起事遍及八州，此標鉅鹿張角起兵處。
confidenceNote.en: The rising spanned eight provinces; the marker sits at Julu, Zhang Jue's base.

summary.zh: 中平元年，太平道張角兄弟舉事，八州響應。亂雖年內大定，朝廷兵權下移州郡，羣雄割據自此始。
summary.en: In 184 the Taiping sect under Zhang Jue rose across eight provinces. The main rising was crushed within the year — but military power passed to the provinces, and the age of warlords began.

summary.zh: 建安五年，曹操與袁紹相持於官渡。操自將步騎五千夜襲烏巢，燒其糧屯；紹將張郃、高覽降，紹軍大潰。史載雙方兵力懸殊，裴松之已疑其不實（見「史料異說」）。
summary.en: In 200 Cao Cao and Yuan Shao faced each other at Guandu. Cao led five thousand men by night against the depot at Wuchao and destroyed the grain; Yuan's generals Zhang He and Gao Lan defected and his army collapsed. The recorded disparity in numbers was doubted even by Pei Songzhi (see "Where the sources disagree").

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷六 魏書 袁紹傳
passages.textZh: 太祖乃留曹洪守，自將步騎五千候夜潛往攻瓊。紹遣騎救之，敗走。破瓊等，悉斬之。
passages.textEn: Taizu left Cao Hong to hold the camp and himself led five thousand foot and horse by night to attack Chunyu Qiong. Shao sent cavalry to the rescue, but they were beaten off. He defeated Qiong and the others and put them all to death.

question.en: How large were the two armies?

claim.zh: 曹軍不滿一萬，傷者十之二三。
claim.en: Cao had under ten thousand men, two or three in ten of them wounded.

source.en: Sanguozhi, Wei 1: Annals of Emperor Wu

accounts.quoteZh: 時公兵不滿萬，傷者十二三。

claim.zh: 裴松之認為曹軍不可能這麼少。
claim.en: Pei Songzhi argued Cao's army cannot have been so small.

accounts.quoteZh: 雖征戰損傷，未應如此之少也。

claim.zh: 袁軍精卒十萬、騎一萬。
claim.en: Yuan had a hundred thousand picked troops and ten thousand horse.

accounts.quoteZh: 簡精卒十萬，騎萬匹，將攻許。

claim.zh: 袁軍步卒五萬、騎八千。
claim.en: Yuan had fifty thousand foot and eight thousand horse.

accounts.quoteZh: 紹步卒五萬，騎八千。

note.zh: 曹弱袁強可信，具體數字不可盡信。
note.en: That Cao was the weaker side is credible; the figures are not.

confidenceNote.zh: 《三國志》只記「赤壁」之名，未明其地；十二月為《武帝紀》所記，相當於西曆208年末至209年初。
confidenceNote.en: The Sanguozhi names Red Cliffs without locating it. The twelfth month given in the Annals of Emperor Wu falls at the turn of 208/209 in the Julian calendar.

summary.zh: 建安十三年冬，曹操既得荊州，自江陵順江東下；孫權、劉備合兵拒之，遇於赤壁。據吳方記載，曹軍船艦首尾相接，黃蓋詐降縱火，延燒岸上營落；曹軍又遭大疫，引軍北還。魏、蜀、吳三方所記各異（見「史料異說」）。南北分立之勢自此而定。
summary.en: In the winter of 208 Cao Cao, having taken Jing Province, moved down the Yangtze from Jiangling. Sun Quan and Liu Bei combined to meet him at Red Cliffs. By the Wu account his ships lay moored bow to stern; Huang Gai feigned surrender and set them alight, and the fire spread to the camps ashore. Struck by epidemic as well, Cao withdrew north. The Wei, Shu and Wu records tell it differently (see "Where the sources disagree"). The south stayed out of his hands.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 公至赤壁，與備戰，不利。於是大疫，吏士多死者，乃引軍還。備遂有荊州、江南諸郡。
passages.textEn: The Duke reached Red Cliffs and engaged Liu Bei, without success. Then a great epidemic broke out and many officers and men died, so he led the army home. Bei thereupon held Jing Province and the commanderies south of the Yangtze.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 與曹公戰於赤壁，大破之，焚其舟船。先主與吳軍水陸並進，追到南郡，時又疾疫，北軍多死，曹公引歸。
passages.textEn: [The First Sovereign] fought Lord Cao at Red Cliffs, routed him utterly and burned his ships. Advancing by water and land together with the Wu army, he pursued him to Nan Commandery; epidemic was again rife, much of the northern army died, and Lord Cao withdrew home.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 吳書 周瑜傳
passages.textZh: 權遂遣瑜及程普等與備並力逆曹公，遇於赤壁。時曹公軍眾已有疾病，初一交戰，公軍敗退，引次江北。瑜等在南岸。瑜部將黃蓋曰：「今寇眾我寡，難與持久。然觀操軍船艦，首尾相接，可燒而走也。」……蓋放諸船，同時發火。時風盛猛，悉延燒岸上營落。頃之，煙炎張天，人馬燒溺死者甚眾，軍遂敗退，還保南郡。
passages.textEn: Sun Quan sent Zhou Yu, Cheng Pu and others to join Liu Bei and meet Lord Cao; they encountered him at Red Cliffs. Cao's host was already sick: at the first clash his army fell back to camp on the north bank, while Yu held the south. Yu's officer Huang Gai said: "The enemy are many and we are few — this cannot be a long contest. But I see Cao's ships lie bow to stern, touching one another: they can be burned and put to flight." … Gai released the ships and they caught fire all at once. The wind blew a gale; the fire spread to the camps on the shore. In moments smoke and flame filled the sky, men and horses burned or drowned in great numbers, and the army fell back in defeat to hold Nan Commandery.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 吳書 吳主傳
passages.textZh: 瑜、普爲左右督，各領萬人，與備俱進，遇於赤壁，大破曹公軍。公燒其餘船引退，士卒饑疫，死者大半。
passages.textEn: Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu, as commanders of the left and right with ten thousand men each, advanced together with Liu Bei and met the enemy at Red Cliffs, where they routed Lord Cao's army. Cao burned his remaining ships and withdrew; his men starved and sickened, and more than half died.

claim.zh: 與劉備交戰不利，繼而大疫，引軍還。不言火攻，也不提周瑜。
claim.en: An unsuccessful engagement with Liu Bei, then an epidemic, then withdrawal. No fire, and no Zhou Yu.

source.en: Sanguozhi, Wei 1: Annals of Emperor Wu

accounts.quoteZh: 公至赤壁，與備戰，不利。於是大疫，吏士多死者，乃引軍還。

claim.zh: 周瑜、程普與劉備並力；黃蓋詐降，縱火焚船，延及岸上營落。
claim.en: Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu with Liu Bei; Huang Gai feigns surrender and fires the fleet, the blaze spreading to the camps ashore.

accounts.quoteZh: 蓋放諸船，同時發火。時風盛猛，悉延燒岸上營落。

claim.zh: 聯軍大破曹軍；曹操自燒餘船而退，士卒饑疫，死者大半。
claim.en: The allies rout Cao, who burns his own remaining ships and withdraws, losing over half his men to hunger and disease.

accounts.quoteZh: 大破曹公軍。公燒其餘船引退，士卒饑疫，死者大半。

claim.zh: 劉備與曹操戰於赤壁，大破之，焚其舟船。
claim.en: Liu Bei fights Cao at Red Cliffs, routs him and burns his ships.

accounts.quoteZh: 與曹公戰於赤壁，大破之，焚其舟船。

claim.zh: 船艦為劉備所燒，曹操從華容道步行而歸。
claim.en: Cao's ships are burned by Liu Bei; he retreats on foot by the Huarong road.

source.en: Shanyang gong zaiji, quoted by Pei Songzhi

accounts.quoteZh: 公船艦爲備所燒，引軍從華容道步歸

note.zh: 三書各為其主：魏書諱敗而歸咎於疫，吳、蜀各自居功。火攻見於吳、蜀兩方記載，船是誰燒的則說法不一。
note.en: Each history favours its own side: the Wei annals play down the defeat and blame disease, while Wu and Shu each take the credit. The fire is attested from both the Wu and Shu sides; who burned which ships is not agreed.

question.zh: 孫權攻合肥，在赤壁之前還是之後？
question.en: Did Sun Quan attack Hefei before or after Red Cliffs?

claim.zh: 之前：孫權先攻合肥，其後曹操才到赤壁。
claim.en: Before: Sun Quan attacks Hefei first, and only then does Cao reach Red Cliffs.

source.en: Sanguozhi, Wei 1: Annals of Emperor Wu

accounts.quoteZh: 十二月，孫權爲備攻合肥。公自江陵征備，至巴丘，遣張憙救合肥。

claim.zh: 之後：破曹之後，孫權自率眾圍合肥，逾月不下。
claim.en: After: once Cao is beaten, Sun Quan himself besieges Hefei for over a month without taking it.

accounts.quoteZh: 權自率眾圍合肥，使張昭攻九江之當塗。昭兵不利，權攻城逾月不能下。

claim.zh: 孫盛比較二說，以吳志為是。
claim.en: Sun Sheng compared the two and judged the Wu record correct.

source.en: Sun Sheng, Yitong ping, quoted by Pei Songzhi

accounts.quoteZh: 案吳志，劉備先破公軍，然後權攻合肥，而此記云權先攻合肥，後有赤壁之事。二者不同，吳志爲是。

claim.zh: 蒲圻（今湖北赤壁市）長江南岸——今多數學者所取，本圖暫從此說。
claim.en: Puqi, on the south bank of the Yangtze (modern Chibi City, Hubei) — the majority view today, followed provisionally on this map.

claim.zh: 另有嘉魚、漢陽、江夏諸說。
claim.en: Jiayu, Hanyang and Jiangxia have also been proposed.

claim.zh: 黃州赤鼻磯——因蘇軾題詠而著名，一般不認為是戰地。
claim.en: Red Nose Rock at Huangzhou — famous from Su Shi's odes, but not generally accepted as the battlefield.

note.zh: 此問題史書無解，圖上以不確定範圍與「址？」標示。
note.en: The histories do not settle this. The map shows an uncertainty halo and marks the site "?".

fiction.zh: 草船借箭、借東風、龐統獻連環計、黃蓋苦肉計、關羽華容道義釋曹操，皆出《三國演義》。史書只說曹軍船艦「首尾相接」，沒有鐵索連船；風向也只見於裴註所引《江表傳》「時東南風急」一語。
fiction.en: Borrowing arrows with straw boats, summoning the east wind, Pang Tong's scheme to chain the ships together, Huang Gai's staged flogging, and Guan Yu sparing Cao Cao on the Huarong road all come from the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The history says only that Cao's ships lay "bow to stern" — no iron chains — and the wind appears in a single phrase of the Jiangbiao zhuan quoted in the commentary.

summary.zh: 建安二十四年，關羽北攻曹仁於樊城。秋，大霖雨，漢水汎溢，于禁所督七軍皆沒，禁降；羽威震華夏，曹操一度議遷許都。呂蒙乘虛，使兵士扮作商人渡江，襲取江陵、公安；羽軍潰散，退保麥城，於臨沮被殺。孫劉聯盟至此破裂。
summary.en: In 219 Guan Yu attacked Cao Ren at Fancheng. Autumn rains flooded the Han River and the seven armies under Yu Jin were lost; Yu Jin surrendered, and Cao Cao briefly considered moving the court from Xu. Lü Meng then slipped down the Yangtze with his soldiers disguised as merchants and took Jiangling and Gong'an behind Guan Yu, whose army dissolved. He fell back to Maicheng and was killed at Linju. The Sun–Liu alliance was finished.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十六 蜀書 關羽傳
passages.textZh: 秋，大霖雨，漢水汎溢，禁所督七軍皆沒。禁降羽，羽又斬將軍龐德。梁、郟、陸渾群盜或遙受羽印號，為之支黨，羽威震華夏。
passages.textEn: In autumn there were heavy rains; the Han River overflowed, and the seven armies under Yu Jin were all lost. Jin surrendered to Yu, who also beheaded General Pang De. Bandits in Liang, Jia and Luhun took his seals and titles from afar and became his partisans; Yu's might shook the realm.

fiction.zh: 《演義》寫關羽築堰蓄水、決堤淹敵（「水淹七軍」）。史書所記只是秋雨水漲，並非人為。
fiction.en: The novel has Guan Yu dam the river and loose it on the enemy ("drowning the seven armies"). The history records only an autumn flood.

summary.zh: 章武元年，劉備東征孫權，自巫峽、建平連營至夷陵界，立數十屯（曹丕聞其「樹柵連營七百餘里」，斷言必敗）。次年，陸遜以火攻破其四十餘營，蜀軍土崩，劉備夜遁入白帝城。
summary.en: In 221 Liu Bei marched east against Sun Quan, stringing dozens of camps from the Wu Gorge and Jianping to the edge of Yiling — Cao Pi, hearing of "palisaded camps for over seven hundred li", predicted defeat. The next year Lu Xun attacked with fire, took more than forty camps, and broke the Shu army. Liu Bei fled by night to Baidicheng.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十八 吳書 陸遜傳
passages.textZh: 乃敕各持一把茅，以火攻拔之。一爾勢成，通率諸軍同時俱攻，斬張南、馮習及胡王沙靡柯等首，破其四十餘營。
passages.textEn: He ordered each man to carry a bundle of thatch and took the camp by fire. Once this succeeded he led all the armies in a general attack, took the heads of Zhang Nan, Feng Xi, the barbarian king Shamoke and others, and broke more than forty camps.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷二 魏書 文帝紀
passages.textZh: 初，帝聞備兵東下，與權交戰，樹柵連營七百餘里，謂羣臣曰：「備不曉兵，豈有七百里營可以拒敵者乎！」
passages.textEn: When the Emperor first heard that Liu Bei had come east to fight Sun Quan, with palisaded camps strung over seven hundred li, he said to his ministers: "Bei does not understand war. Who ever held off an enemy with seven hundred li of camps?"

fiction.zh: 「火燒連營七百里」是後世說法：「七百里」出自曹丕之語，陸遜傳所記戰果為「破其四十餘營」。
fiction.en: "Burning seven hundred li of camps" is a later conflation: the seven hundred li is Cao Pi's remark, while Lu Xun's biography records "more than forty camps" taken.

confidenceNote.zh: 五次用兵路線各異，此標祁山方面。
confidenceNote.en: Five campaigns took different routes; the marker sits on the Qishan axis.

summary.zh: 建興六年至十二年，諸葛亮五次北伐曹魏：兩出祁山，一圍陳倉，一取武都、陰平，末次出斜谷、據五丈原。主力數次皆因糧運不繼而還。
summary.en: Between 228 and 234 Zhuge Liang launched five campaigns against Wei: two by Qishan, one against Chencang, one that took Wudu and Yinping, and a last through the Xie Valley to the Wuzhang Plains. Supply defeated each of the main thrusts.

summary.zh: 諸葛亮最後一次北伐，與司馬懿對峙渭南百餘日；八月，亮卒於軍中，蜀師退還。
summary.en: Zhuge Liang's final expedition stalled facing Sima Yi south of the Wei River for over a hundred days; in the autumn of 234 he died in camp and the Shu army withdrew.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十五 蜀書 諸葛亮傳
passages.textZh: 十二年春，亮悉大眾由斜谷出，以流馬運，據武功五丈原，與司馬宣王對於渭南。
passages.textEn: In the spring of the twelfth year Liang brought out his whole host by the Xie Valley, supplied by "flowing horse" transports, took position at the Wuzhang Plains in Wugong, and faced Sima Yi south of the Wei River.

fiction.zh: 禳星延壽為小說情節。「死諸葛走生仲達」是當時百姓的諺語，見裴註所引《漢晉春秋》；「有星墜於亮營」亦出裴註引《晉陽秋》，均非陳壽本文。
fiction.en: The lamp ritual to prolong his life is the novel's. "A dead Zhuge scares off a living Zhongda" was a popular saying, recorded in the Han Jin chunqiu quoted by Pei; the star falling on his camp is likewise from the commentary (Jin yangqiu), not Chen Shou's text.

confidenceNote.zh: 三路進兵，此標成都受降處。
confidenceNote.en: A three-pronged campaign; the marker sits at Chengdu, where Shu surrendered.

summary.zh: 景元四年，鍾會主力攻劍閣，鄧艾偷渡陰平，出其不意兵臨成都，後主劉禪出降，蜀漢亡。
summary.en: In 263 Zhong Hui pinned the Shu army at Jiange while Deng Ai crossed the trackless Yinping mountains and appeared before Chengdu. Liu Shan surrendered, ending Shu Han.

summary.zh: 咸寧五年晉六路伐吳，王濬樓船自益州順流而下，直抵建業；太康元年孫皓出降，天下復歸一統。
summary.en: In 279–280 Jin attacked Wu along six routes; Wang Jun's river fleet swept down the Yangtze from Sichuan to Jianye. Sun Hao surrendered in 280, reunifying the empire.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年無確載。
confidenceNote.en: Birth year not reliably recorded.

summary.zh: 涼州軍閥。中平六年率兵入洛陽，廢少帝、立獻帝；關東兵起，焚洛陽、挾帝西遷長安。初平三年為王允、呂布所殺，部將李傕、郭汜續據關中。
summary.en: A Liang-province general who marched into Luoyang in 189, deposed one emperor and enthroned another. Facing the eastern coalition he burned Luoyang and dragged the court to Chang'an; he was assassinated in 192, and his officers Li Jue and Guo Si held Guanzhong after him.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷六 魏書 董卓傳
passages.textZh: 初平元年二月，乃徙天子都長安。焚燒洛陽宮室，悉發掘陵墓，取寶物。
passages.textEn: In the second month of the first year of Chuping he moved the Son of Heaven's capital to Chang'an, burned the palaces of Luoyang, and dug up all the tombs for their treasures.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年無確載；卒於建安三年十二月，約當西曆199年初。
confidenceNote.en: Birth year unrecorded; executed in the twelfth month of Jian'an 3, early 199 by the Julian calendar.

summary.zh: 并州武將，「便弓馬，膂力過人，號為飛將」。先事丁原而殺之，歸董卓；後又與王允謀殺卓。興平元年襲取兗州大部，後奪劉備之徐州；建安三年曹操圍下邳，決泗、沂水灌城，部將執陳宮出降，布被擒殺。
summary.en: A cavalry officer from Bing province, "skilled with bow and horse, stronger than other men, called the Flying General". He served Ding Yuan and killed him to join Dong Zhuo, then joined Wang Yun's plot to kill Dong Zhuo. He seized most of Yan province in 194 and later took Xu province from Liu Bei, until Cao Cao flooded Xiapi; his officers handed over Chen Gong and the city, and he was captured and executed.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷七 魏書 呂布傳
passages.textZh: 布便弓馬，膂力過人，號為飛將。
passages.textEn: Bu was skilled with bow and horse and stronger than other men; he was called the Flying General.

fiction.zh: 貂蟬與「連環計」、虎牢關「三英戰呂布」皆小說情節。史書只說呂布「與卓侍婢私通，恐事發覺，心不自安」。轅門射戟則確有其事，見本傳。
fiction.en: Diaochan and the "chain scheme", and the three heroes fighting Lü Bu at Hulao Pass, are the novel's. The history says only that he "had an affair with one of Dong Zhuo's maids and feared discovery". The archery feat at the camp gate, on the other hand, is in his biography.

summary.zh: 袁紹從弟。初據南陽，後徙淮南，都壽春。建安二年僭號稱帝，眾叛親離，四年窮蹙病卒。
summary.en: Yuan Shao's cousin and rival. Based first at Nanyang, then in Huainan with his seat at Shouchun, he declared himself emperor in 197 — and was abandoned by nearly everyone, dying destitute in 199.

summary.zh: 遼西人，邊地武將。殺幽州牧劉虞而據其地，與袁紹爭河北；界橋敗後退保易京，築圍塹十重，積穀三百萬斛。建安四年袁紹掘地道壞其樓，瓚盡殺妻子而自殺。
summary.en: A frontier commander from Liaoxi. He killed Governor Liu Yu to take You province and fought Yuan Shao for the north; beaten at Jieqiao, he withdrew into the fortress of Yijing behind ten rings of moats, with three million hu of grain. In 199 Yuan Shao's sappers brought down his towers; he killed his wife and children and then himself.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷八 魏書 公孫瓚傳
passages.textZh: 瓚自知必敗，盡殺其妻子，乃自殺。
passages.textEn: Knowing defeat was certain, Zan killed his wife and children and then took his own life.

claim.zh: 殺妻子後自殺。
claim.en: He killed his family and then himself.

accounts.quoteZh: 瓚自知必敗，盡殺其妻子，乃自殺。

claim.zh: 引火自焚——見於後出的《後漢書》，本圖未及核對原文。
claim.en: He set fire to his tower and burned — the version in the later Hou Hanshu, not yet checked against its text for this atlas.

summary.zh: 漢室宗親，初平元年為荊州刺史，治襄陽。保境安民近二十年，荊州成為亂世樂土；建安十三年病卒，子琮舉州降曹。
summary.en: An imperial clansman who governed Jing province from Xiangyang for nearly two decades, keeping it an island of peace and learning. He died in 208 just as Cao Cao marched south, and his son Liu Cong surrendered the province.

summary.zh: 益州牧劉焉之子，興平元年嗣位。闇弱無斷，引劉備入蜀以拒張魯，反為所圖；建安十九年成都被圍，出降。
summary.en: Son of Liu Yan, whom he succeeded as governor of Yi province in 194. Weak and irresolute, he invited Liu Bei in to fight Zhang Lu — and lost his province to his guest, surrendering Chengdu in 214.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十一 蜀書 劉璋傳
passages.textZh: 璋言：「父子在州二十餘年，無恩德以加百姓。百姓攻戰三年，肌膏草野者，以璋故也，何心能安！」遂開城出降，群下莫不流涕。
passages.textEn: Zhang said: "My father and I have held this province for over twenty years without doing the people any kindness. For three years they have fought, and it is on my account that their flesh enriches the fields. How could I be at peace?" He opened the gates and surrendered; among his officers there was none who did not weep.

summary.zh: 五斗米道首領。初平二年據漢中，「以鬼道教民，自號師君」，不置長吏，以祭酒為治，「雄據巴、漢垂三十年」。建安二十年曹操來伐，封藏府庫而去，後出降。
summary.en: Leader of the Five Pecks of Rice sect. He seized Hanzhong in 191, "taught the people by the way of spirits and styled himself Master-Lord", governing through his priests instead of officials — "master of Ba and Han for nearly thirty years". When Cao Cao invaded in 215 he sealed his treasuries intact before withdrawing, and then surrendered.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷八 魏書 張魯傳
passages.textZh: 魯遂據漢中，以鬼道教民，自號「師君」。……雄據巴、漢垂三十年。
passages.textEn: Lu then held Hanzhong, taught the people by the way of spirits, and styled himself "Master-Lord". … He was master of Ba and Han for nearly thirty years.

summary.zh: 馬騰之子。建安十六年與韓遂及關中諸將進軍潼關拒曹，為賈詡離間之計所破，敗走隴上；後投劉備，為蜀漢驃騎將軍。
summary.en: Son of Ma Teng. With Han Sui and the Guanzhong warlords he advanced to Tong Pass against Cao Cao in 211, was undone when Jia Xu's stratagem set him and Han Sui against each other, and was driven back to Longyou. He ended his career in Liu Bei's service.

summary.zh: 孫堅長子，孫權之兄。興平二年渡江，「轉鬥所向皆破」，數年間略定丹陽、吳、會稽、豫章，奠定江東基業。建安五年為故吳郡太守許貢的門客所傷而卒，年二十六。
summary.en: Sun Jian's eldest son and Sun Quan's brother. Crossing the Yangtze in 195 he "fought his way forward and broke all before him", conquering Danyang, Wu, Kuaiji and Yuzhang within five years and founding the Sun family's state. In 200 he was wounded by retainers of Xu Gong, a governor he had killed, and died aged twenty-six by Chinese reckoning.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十六 吳書 孫策傳
passages.textZh: 渡江轉鬥，所向皆破。莫敢當其鋒，而軍令整肅，百姓懷之。
passages.textEn: He crossed the river and fought his way forward, breaking all before him. None dared face him, yet his army was strictly disciplined and the people took to him.

summary.zh: 中平六年為遼東太守，乘中原大亂自立為遼東侯、平州牧。子康、孫淵相繼，割據遼東、玄菟、樂浪近五十年，至景初二年為司馬懿所滅。
summary.en: Appointed governor of Liaodong in 189, he made himself effectively independent as the heartland collapsed. His son Gongsun Kang and grandson Gongsun Yuan kept Liaodong, Xuantu and Lelang as a family domain for nearly fifty years, until Sima Yi destroyed it in 238.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷八 魏書 公孫度傳
passages.textZh: 自立為遼東侯、平州牧，追封父延為建義侯。
passages.textEn: He set himself up as Marquis of Liaodong and Governor of Ping province, and posthumously enfeoffed his father Yan as Marquis of Jianyi.

summary.zh: 交趾太守，兄弟並領交州諸郡，保境四十年，中原士人多往依之。建安十五年附孫權；黃武五年卒，吳遂收交州。
summary.en: Governor of Jiaozhi, whose brothers held the neighbouring commanderies. For forty years the far south under his family was a haven for refugees from the north. He submitted to Sun Quan in 210 while remaining autonomous; on his death in 226 Wu took direct control.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十九 吳書 士燮傳
passages.textZh: 燮在郡四十餘歲，黃武五年，年九十卒。
passages.textEn: Xie held the commandery for over forty years and died in the fifth year of Huangwu, aged ninety.

summary.zh: 徐州牧。曹操之父曹嵩在其境內遇害，操因此兩度東征，所過殘戮；誰殺了曹嵩，各書說法不同（見「史料異說」）。興平元年病死，臨終稱「非劉備不能安此州」。
summary.en: Governor of Xu province. Cao Cao's father Cao Song was killed in his territory, and Cao Cao twice invaded in revenge, devastating the province; the sources disagree about who killed him (see "Where the sources disagree"). Tao Qian died of illness in 194, saying on his deathbed that only Liu Bei could keep the province safe.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 謙病篤，謂別駕麋竺曰：「非劉備不能安此州也。」
passages.textEn: When Qian was gravely ill he said to his aide Mi Zhu: "No one but Liu Bei can keep this province safe."

claim.zh: 為陶謙所害，曹操因而東征復仇。
claim.en: Killed by Tao Qian, which is why Cao Cao marched east for revenge.

source.en: Sanguozhi, Wei 1: Annals of Emperor Wu

accounts.quoteZh: 太祖父嵩去官後還譙，董卓之亂，避難琅邪，爲陶謙所害，故太祖志在復讎東伐。

claim.zh: 陶謙密遣數千騎掩捕，曹嵩全家被殺。
claim.en: Tao Qian secretly sent several thousand horsemen to seize the family, and all were killed.

accounts.quoteZh: 陶謙密遣數千騎掩捕。……嵩逃于厠，與妾俱被害，闔門皆死。

claim.zh: 陶謙派都尉張闓護送，張闓見財起意殺曹嵩，逃往淮南；曹操歸咎於陶謙。
claim.en: Tao Qian sent an officer, Zhang Kai, as escort. Zhang Kai murdered Cao Song for his goods and fled to Huainan; Cao Cao blamed Tao Qian.

source.en: Wei Yao, Wu shu, quoted by Pei Songzhi

accounts.quoteZh: 陶謙遣都尉張闓將騎二百衞送，闓於泰山華、費間殺嵩，取財物，因奔淮南。太祖歸咎於陶謙，故伐之。

note.zh: 陶謙是主使還是受累，史無定論。
note.en: Whether Tao Qian ordered the killing or merely took the blame is not settled.

summary.zh: 魏之重臣。拒諸葛亮於渭南，平公孫淵於遼東；正始十年發動高平陵之變，誅曹爽，魏政自此歸司馬氏，其孫炎遂代魏建晉。
summary.en: Wei's leading general and statesman. He held off Zhuge Liang on the Wei River and destroyed the Gongsun regime in Liaodong; his coup of 249 put the Wei court in his family's hands, and his grandson Sima Yan founded the Jin.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年無確載；卒於建安二十四年十二月，約當西曆220年初。
confidenceNote.en: Birth year unrecorded; killed in the twelfth month of Jian'an 24, around the turn of 219/220.

summary.zh: 劉備麾下大將，留鎮荊州。建安二十四年北攻樊城，值漢水汎溢，于禁七軍皆沒，威震華夏；呂蒙襲其後方，軍散，退保麥城，於臨沮為吳將所殺。
summary.en: Liu Bei's foremost general, left to hold Jing province. In 219 he besieged Fancheng; when the Han River flooded, Yu Jin's seven armies were lost and Guan Yu's name shook the north — until Lü Meng seized Jing behind him. His army melted away; he fell back to Maicheng and was killed at Linju.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十六 蜀書 關羽傳
passages.textZh: 先主與二人寢則同床，恩若兄弟。
passages.textEn: The First Sovereign shared a bed with the two of them [Guan Yu and Zhang Fei], with the affection of brothers.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十六 蜀書 關羽傳
passages.textZh: 權遣將逆擊羽，斬羽及子平於臨沮。
passages.textEn: Sun Quan sent officers to intercept Yu, and beheaded him and his son Ping at Linju.

fiction.zh: 桃園結義、過五關斬六將、華容道釋曹操，皆小說情節。史書只說劉、關、張「恩若兄弟」。
fiction.en: The Peach Garden oath, the ride through five passes, and the release of Cao Cao at Huarong are the novel's. The history says only that Liu, Guan and Zhang were "like brothers".

summary.zh: 初平三年，袁紹與公孫瓚爭冀州，戰於界橋。本傳只記瓚「進軍界橋」而敗；戰陣細節——麴義以八百人為先登、強弩千張夾擊、大破瓚之騎兵——出自裴註所引《英雄記》。
summary.en: In 192 Yuan Shao met Gongsun Zan at Jieqiao for control of Ji province. The biographies themselves record little more than the advance and the defeat; the tactical detail — Qu Yi's eight hundred men in the van, flanked by a thousand crossbows, breaking Gongsun Zan's cavalry — comes from the Yingxiong ji quoted in Pei Songzhi's commentary.

confidenceNote.zh: 界橋確址不詳，約在廣宗以東的清河上。
confidenceNote.en: The exact site of Jieqiao is unknown; it lay on the Qing River somewhere east of Guangzong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷六 魏書 袁紹傳 裴註引《英雄記》
passages.textZh: 紹令麴義以八百兵爲先登，彊弩千張夾承之，紹自以步兵數萬結陣於後。……義兵皆伏楯下不動，未至數十步，乃同時俱起，揚塵大叫，直前衝突，彊弩雷發，所中必倒。
passages.textEn: Shao ordered Qu Yi to lead with eight hundred men, a thousand crossbows supporting them on either side, while he himself drew up tens of thousands of infantry behind. … Yi's men lay still beneath their shields; when the enemy was within a few dozen paces they rose all at once, raising the dust with a great shout, and charged straight in as the crossbows thundered; whatever they hit went down.

summary.zh: 建安三年冬，曹操圍呂布於下邳，引泗、沂之水灌城。布眾離心，部將縛陳宮以降，布亦被擒處死。
summary.en: In the winter of 198 Cao Cao besieged Lü Bu in Xiapi and turned the Si and Yi rivers into the city. Lü Bu's officers mutinied; he was captured and executed.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 用荀攸、郭嘉計，遂決泗、沂水以灌城。月餘，布將宋憲、魏續等執陳宮，舉城降，生禽布、宮，皆殺之。
passages.textEn: On the advice of Xun You and Guo Jia he breached the Si and Yi rivers to flood the city. After more than a month Bu's officers Song Xian, Wei Xu and others seized Chen Gong and surrendered the city. Bu and Gong were taken alive, and both were put to death.

summary.zh: 公孫瓚築易京，為圍塹十重，積穀三百萬斛以自守。袁紹掘地道，突壞其樓；建安四年城陷，瓚自殺，紹遂兼有四州。
summary.en: Gongsun Zan shut himself in the fortress of Yijing behind ten rings of moats, with three million hu of grain. Yuan Shao's sappers tunnelled under his towers; when the fortress fell in 199 Gongsun Zan killed himself, leaving Yuan Shao master of four provinces.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷八 魏書 公孫瓚傳
passages.textZh: 為圍塹十重，於塹裡築京，皆高五六丈，為樓其上；中塹為京，特高十丈，自居焉，積穀三百萬斛。
passages.textEn: He dug ten rings of moat and raised mounds within them, each fifty or sixty feet high, with towers on top. The mound at the centre was a hundred feet high; there he lived himself, with three million hu of grain in store.

summary.zh: 建安十二年，曹操出盧龍塞，塹山堙谷五百餘里，奇襲烏桓。張遼陣斬蹋頓，袁氏殘餘與三郡烏桓俱平，北方始定。
summary.en: In 207 Cao Cao led a forced march through the Lulong Pass and five hundred li of trackless hills to surprise the Wuhuan. Zhang Liao killed their chief Tadun in the field, ending both the Wuhuan threat and the last of the Yuan family.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 引軍出盧龍塞，塞外道絕不通，乃壍山堙谷五百餘里，經白檀，歷平岡，涉鮮卑庭，東指柳城。
passages.textEn: He led the army out through the Lulong Pass. Beyond it the road was cut and impassable, so they cut through hills and filled valleys for over five hundred li, by way of Baitan and Pinggang, across the Xianbei grounds, heading east for Liucheng.

summary.zh: 建安十三年秋，劉備攜民南走江陵，曹操精騎一日一夜行三百里，追及於當陽長坂。備棄妻子走，張飛據水斷橋，趙雲救出後主。
summary.en: In autumn 208 Liu Bei fled south with a column of refugees. Cao Cao's picked cavalry covered three hundred li in a day and a night and caught him at Changban; Liu Bei escaped with a handful of riders while Zhang Fei held the bridge.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 曹公將精騎五千急追之，一日一夜行三百餘里，及於當陽之長坂。先主棄妻子，與諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲等數十騎走，曹公大獲其人眾輜重。
passages.textEn: Lord Cao took five thousand picked cavalry in hot pursuit, covering over three hundred li in a day and a night, and caught him at Changban in Dangyang. The First Sovereign abandoned his wife and children and fled with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun and a few dozen riders; Lord Cao took great numbers of his people and baggage.

summary.zh: 建安十六年，馬超、韓遂與關中諸將進軍潼關拒曹操。操潛遣徐晃、朱靈夜渡蒲阪津，據河西為營，自潼關北渡；又用賈詡之謀離間超、遂，大破之，關中遂平。
summary.en: In 211 Ma Chao, Han Sui and the other Guanzhong warlords advanced to Tong Pass against Cao Cao. He sent Xu Huang and Zhu Ling across the Yellow River at Puban by night to hold the west bank, crossed north himself, and on Jia Xu's advice sowed distrust between Ma Chao and Han Sui before shattering the coalition and taking Guanzhong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十六 蜀書 馬超傳
passages.textZh: 曹公用賈詡謀，離間超、遂，更相猜疑，軍以大敗。
passages.textEn: Lord Cao used Jia Xu's stratagem to estrange Chao and Sui. Each grew suspicious of the other, and their army was badly defeated.

summary.zh: 建安二十年，孫權圍合肥，《張遼傳》稱其眾十萬。張遼夜募敢死之士八百人，平旦突陣，直抵孫權麾下；權退軍時又在逍遙津遭遼襲擊，幾不得脫。
summary.en: In 215 Sun Quan besieged Hefei — with a hundred thousand men, according to Zhang Liao's biography. Zhang Liao raised eight hundred volunteers overnight, charged at dawn as far as Sun Quan's own standard, and then struck the retreat at Xiaoyao Ford, nearly taking Sun Quan himself.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷十七 魏書 張遼傳
passages.textZh: 遼夜募敢從之士，得八百人，椎牛饗將士，明日大戰。平旦，遼被甲持戟，先登陷陳，殺數十人，斬二將，大呼自名，衝壘入，至權麾下。
passages.textEn: That night Liao called for men who dared follow him and got eight hundred. He slaughtered oxen to feast them for the next day's battle. At dawn, in armour and halberd in hand, he was first into the enemy line, killed dozens, cut down two officers, shouted his own name, and broke through the ramparts to Sun Quan's standard.

summary.zh: 建安二十二年至二十四年，劉備爭漢中。黃忠於定軍山陣斬夏侯淵；曹操親至，相持數月不能下，引軍還，備遂稱漢中王。
summary.en: From 217 to 219 Liu Bei fought for Hanzhong. Huang Zhong killed Xiahou Yuan at Mount Dingjun; Cao Cao came in person, failed to dislodge the Shu army after months of stalemate, and withdrew. Liu Bei proclaimed himself King of Hanzhong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 二十四年春，自陽平南渡沔水，緣山稍前，於定軍山勢作營。淵將兵來爭其地。先主命黃忠乘高鼓譟攻之，大破淵軍，斬淵。
passages.textEn: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year he crossed the Mian River south from Yangping, advanced along the hills, and made camp on the slopes of Mount Dingjun. Xiahou Yuan brought troops to contest the ground. The First Sovereign ordered Huang Zhong to attack from the height with drums and shouting; he routed Yuan's army and killed Yuan.

confidenceNote.zh: 三路進兵，此標味縣一帶。
confidenceNote.en: A three-column campaign; the marker sits near Wei county.

summary.zh: 建興三年，諸葛亮五月渡瀘，分三路南征，平雍闓、高定、朱褒之亂，分置建寧、雲南、興古諸郡，以夷帥治之。
summary.en: In 225 Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu River and marched south in three columns against the rebels Yong Kai, Gao Ding and Zhu Bao. He reorganized the region into new commanderies and left it under local chiefs.

question.en: Were there "seven captures of Meng Huo"?

claim.zh: 本文只記當年秋天平定，未提孟獲。
claim.en: Chen Shou's text says only that the south was pacified by autumn. Meng Huo is not mentioned.

accounts.quoteZh: 三年春，亮率眾南征，其秋悉平。

claim.zh: 七縱七擒，孟獲心服，南人不復反。
claim.en: Captured and released seven times, until Meng Huo submitted and the south rebelled no more.

source.en: Han Jin chunqiu, quoted by Pei Songzhi

accounts.quoteZh: 縱使更戰，七縱七禽，而亮猶遣獲。

note.zh: 此事只見於後出之書，次數尤其可疑。
note.en: The story appears only in a later work; the number in particular is doubtful.

confidenceNote.zh: 街亭確址有秦安隴城、莊浪諸說。
confidenceNote.en: The site of Jieting is disputed (Longcheng in Qin'an vs. Zhuanglang).

summary.zh: 建興六年第一次北伐，南安、天水、安定三郡叛魏應亮。馬謖為先鋒，捨水上山，不據城；張郃絕其汲道，大破之。諸葛亮進無所據，退還漢中。馬謖的結局，史文不一（見「史料異說」）。
summary.en: During the first northern expedition in 228 the commanderies of Nan'an, Tianshui and Anding went over to Shu. Ma Su, commanding the van, left the water and camped on a height instead of holding the town; Zhang He cut off his water and routed him. With nowhere to anchor his advance, Zhuge Liang withdrew to Hanzhong. The sources differ on Ma Su's fate (see "Where the sources disagree").

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十三 蜀書 王平傳
passages.textZh: 謖捨水上山，舉措煩擾，平連規諫謖，謖不能用，大敗於街亭。
passages.textEn: Su left the water and went up the hill, and his dispositions were confused. Ping remonstrated again and again; Su would not listen, and was badly beaten at Jieting.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷十七 魏書 張郃傳
passages.textZh: 謖依阻南山，不下據城。郃絶其汲道，擊，大破之。
passages.textEn: Su relied on the southern hills and did not come down to hold the town. He cut off his water supply, attacked, and routed him.

claim.zh: 被處死，以謝眾人。
claim.en: Executed, to answer to the army.

accounts.quoteZh: 戮謖以謝眾。

claim.zh: 與將軍張休、李盛一同被誅。
claim.en: Put to death together with the generals Zhang Xiu and Li Sheng.

accounts.quoteZh: 丞相亮既誅馬謖及將軍張休、李盛

claim.zh: 下獄而死；諸葛亮為之流涕。
claim.en: Died in prison; Zhuge Liang wept for him.

source.en: Sanguozhi, Shu 9: Ma Liang (Ma Su appended)

accounts.quoteZh: 謖下獄物故，亮為之流涕。

claim.zh: 兵敗後曾逃亡；向朗知情不報，因而免官。
claim.en: He fled after the defeat; Xiang Lang knew and did not report it, and was dismissed.

accounts.quoteZh: 朗素與馬謖善，謖逃亡，朗知情不舉，亮恨之，免官還成都。

note.zh: 四條可以並存——先逃亡，被捕下獄，定罪而死——但史文並未說明。「物故」只言其死，不言死法。
note.en: The four can be reconciled — flight, arrest, a death sentence, death in custody or by execution — but the text does not say so. "物故" states only that he died, not how.

fiction.zh: 街亭失守後諸葛亮以「空城計」嚇退司馬懿，為小說情節。此役魏方主將是張郃；據裴松之考辨，司馬懿當時在荊州。
fiction.en: The empty-fort ruse against Sima Yi after the fall of Jieting is the novel's. The Wei commander here was Zhang He; as Pei Songzhi pointed out, Sima Yi was then in Jing province.

summary.zh: 黃武七年，吳鄱陽太守周魴詐降誘敵。魏大司馬曹休信之，「帥步騎十萬」深入皖地；陸遜等橫截其軍，大破之於石亭。
summary.en: In 228 the Wu officer Zhou Fang feigned defection. Cao Xiu believed him and marched "a hundred thousand foot and horse" deep toward Wan; Lu Xun cut across his column and routed him at Shiting.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷六十 吳書 周魴傳
passages.textZh: 休果信魴，帥步騎十萬，輜重滿道，逕來入皖。魴亦合眾，隨陸遜橫截休，休幅裂瓦解，斬獲萬計。
passages.textEn: Xiu did believe Fang. With a hundred thousand foot and horse, his baggage filling the roads, he marched straight into Wan. Fang gathered his own men and with Lu Xun cut across Xiu's column; it was torn apart, with tens of thousands killed or taken.

summary.zh: 景初二年，司馬懿征公孫淵，圍襄平。會霖雨三十餘日，遼水暴漲；雨止後起土山、發石連弩攻城。城中糧盡，淵突圍，被斬，遼東、帶方、樂浪、玄菟悉平，公孫氏三世之業遂亡。
summary.en: In 238 Sima Yi marched against Gongsun Yuan and besieged Xiangping. It rained for more than thirty days and the Liao River rose; when the rain stopped he raised mounds and battered the city with catapults and repeating crossbows. With the food gone Gongsun Yuan tried to break out and was killed. Liaodong, Daifang, Lelang and Xuantu submitted, ending the family's three-generation domain.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷八 魏書 公孫度傳附公孫淵
passages.textZh: 會霖雨三十餘日，遼水暴長，運船自遼口徑至城下。雨霽，起土山、脩櫓，為發石連弩射城中。淵窘急。糧盡，人相食，死者甚多。
passages.textEn: It rained for more than thirty days; the Liao River rose so that supply ships came from its mouth straight to the city walls. When the rain cleared they raised mounds and towers and shot into the city with stone-throwers and repeating crossbows. Yuan was hard pressed. The grain ran out, people ate one another, and very many died.

summary.zh: 建興元年冬，孫權新喪，魏三道伐吳。諸葛恪救東興，丁奉雪中解甲短兵奮擊，大破魏軍，死者數萬。
summary.en: In the winter of 252, just after Sun Quan's death, Wei attacked on three fronts. At Dongxing, Ding Feng's men stripped off their armour in the snow and stormed the Wei camp with short swords, routing it.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十五 吳書 丁奉傳
passages.textZh: 天寒雪，敵諸將置酒高會，奉見其前部兵少，……乃使兵解鎧著冑，持短兵。敵人從而笑焉，不爲設備。奉縱兵斫之，大破敵前屯。
passages.textEn: It was cold and snowing, and the enemy commanders were feasting. Feng saw that their forward troops were few … and had his men take off their armour, keep their helmets, and carry short blades. The enemy laughed and took no precautions. Feng loosed his men on them and broke the forward camp.

summary.zh: 甘露二年五月，魏征東大將軍諸葛誕被徵為司空，疑懼而反，據壽春，引吳為援。司馬昭督中外諸軍二十六萬圍之；次年城破，誕突圍被斬，夷三族。淮南三次叛亂至此而終。
summary.en: In 257 the Wei general Zhuge Dan, summoned to court and fearing for himself, rebelled at Shouchun and called in Wu. Sima Zhao brought 260,000 men to besiege the city. It fell the next year; Zhuge Dan was cut down trying to break out, and his clan exterminated — the last of the three Huainan revolts.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷二十八 魏書 諸葛誕傳
passages.textZh: 大將軍司馬文王督中外諸軍二十六萬眾，臨淮討之。
passages.textEn: The General-in-Chief, Sima Zhao, led 260,000 men of the central and provincial armies to the Huai to put him down.

summary.zh: 鳳皇元年，吳西陵督步闡據城降晉。陸抗築圍，內以困闡、外以禦寇，擊退晉軍來援，拔西陵。吳之西門得以再保八年。
summary.en: In 272 the Wu commander Bu Chan defected to Jin with the fortress of Xiling. Lu Kang ringed the city with works facing both inward and outward, beat off the Jin relief, and retook it — keeping Wu's western gate shut for eight more years.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十八 吳書 陸遜傳附陸抗
passages.textZh: 鳳皇元年，西陵督步闡據城以叛，遣使降晉。……敕軍營更築嚴圍，自赤谿至故市，內以圍闡，外以禦寇。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Fenghuang, Bu Chan, commander at Xiling, rebelled with the city and sent envoys to submit to Jin. … [Lu Kang] ordered the army to build strict siege lines from Chixi to Gushi, enclosing Chan within and holding off the enemy without.

summary.zh: 洛陽、長安相繼陷落後，琅邪王司馬睿在建康即晉王位（317），次年稱帝，晉室偏安江左。北方流民大量南渡，世家大族與皇權共治，時稱「王與馬，共天下」。淝水一戰保住江南；元熙二年（420）劉裕受禪，晉亡。
summary.en: After Luoyang and Chang'an fell, Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, took the title King of Jin at Jiankang (317) and emperor the next year, and the Jin court lived on south of the Yangtze. Refugees poured south; great families shared power with the throne — "the Wang and the Ma share the realm". The Fei River (383) kept the south safe; in 420 Liu Yu took the abdication and Jin ended.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 羣臣乃不敢逼，請依魏晉故事爲晉王，許之。辛卯，卽王位，大赦，改元。
passages.textEn: The ministers then dared not press him further, and asked that he become King of Jin after the precedents of Wei and Jin; he agreed. On xinmao he took the royal title, proclaimed an amnesty and changed the era name.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 傅亮承裕密旨，諷帝禪位，草詔，請帝書之。帝欣然謂左右曰：「晉氏久已失之，今復何恨。」乃書赤紙爲詔。
passages.textEn: Fu Liang, carrying out Liu Yu's secret instructions, hinted to the emperor that he should abdicate, drafted the edict and asked him to write it out. The emperor said cheerfully to those around him: "The house of Jin lost this long ago — what is there to regret now?" And he wrote the edict on red paper.

summary.zh: 匈奴劉淵以漢室外甥自居，304年稱漢王於左國城，後徙平陽。其子劉聰時陷洛陽（311）、長安（316），俘懷、愍二帝。劉曜改國號為趙（史稱前趙），329年為石勒所滅。
summary.en: The Xiongnu leader Liu Yuan, claiming descent from Han princesses, took the title King of Han at Zuoguocheng in 304 and later moved to Pingyang. Under his son Liu Cong his armies took Luoyang (311) and Chang'an (316) and captured two Jin emperors. Liu Yao renamed the state Zhao (the "Former Zhao"); Shi Le destroyed it in 329.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零一 劉元海載記
passages.textZh: 吾又漢氏之甥，約為兄弟，兄亡弟紹，不亦可乎？且可稱漢，追尊後主，以懷人望。
passages.textEn: "I am, besides, a nephew of the house of Han, bound to it as a brother; when the elder brother dies the younger carries on — is that not fitting? Let us call ourselves Han and posthumously honour the Later Sovereign, to win men's hopes."

summary.zh: 羯人石勒原為漢趙部將，319年自稱趙王於襄國，329年滅前趙，據有北方大部。石虎遷都鄴，其死後（349）諸子相殘，冉閔奪權，國遂崩潰。
summary.en: Shi Le, a Jie chieftain who began as a general of Han-Zhao, declared himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo in 319 and destroyed the Former Zhao in 329, holding most of the north. Shi Hu moved the capital to Ye; after his death in 349 his sons fought each other, Ran Min seized power, and the state collapsed.

summary.zh: 巴氐李特率流民入蜀，其子李雄304年據成都，306年稱帝，國號成，李壽時改號漢。永和三年（347）桓溫溯江入蜀，滅之。
summary.en: Li Te led refugees from the north-west into Sichuan; his son Li Xiong took Chengdu in 304 and called himself emperor of Cheng in 306 (renamed Han under Li Shou). Huan Wen came up the Yangtze and destroyed it in 347.

confidenceNote.en: Borders in the Sixteen Kingdoms period are recorded at key dates only and are approximate.

summary.zh: 鮮卑慕容部在遼西、遼東崛起，337年慕容皝稱燕王，341年遷都龍城。後趙崩潰後南下取鄴（352），慕容儁稱帝。370年為前秦所滅。
summary.en: The Murong Xianbei rose in Liaoxi and Liaodong; Murong Huang took the title King of Yan in 337 and moved to Longcheng in 341. When Later Zhao collapsed they came south and took Ye (352), and Murong Jun proclaimed himself emperor. Former Qin destroyed the state in 370.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零九 慕容皝載記
passages.textZh: 使陽裕、唐柱等築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣。
passages.textEn: He had Yang Yu, Tang Zhu and others build Longcheng, raise palaces and temples, and renamed Liucheng county Longcheng.
