confidenceNote.en: Borders in the Sixteen Kingdoms period are recorded at key dates only and are approximate.

summary.zh: 氐人苻氏所建，都長安。苻堅任用王猛，先後滅前燕（370）、前涼與代（376），統一北方。383年大舉南伐，敗於淝水，國隨之瓦解。
summary.en: Founded by the Di Fu clan at Chang'an. Fu Jian, with Wang Meng as his minister, destroyed Former Yan (370), Former Liang and Dai (376) and united the north. His great southern campaign of 383 broke at the Fei River, and the state fell apart.

confidenceNote.zh: 十六國時期疆域只錄關鍵年份，為約略復原。
confidenceNote.en: Borders in the Sixteen Kingdoms period are recorded at key dates only and are approximate.

summary.zh: 淝水戰後慕容垂復燕，都中山。396年後北魏南下，奪并州、中山與鄴，後燕退保龍城，407年為北燕所代。
summary.en: After the Fei River Murong Chui restored Yan with its capital at Zhongshan. From 396 Northern Wei took Bing Province, Zhongshan and Ye; Later Yan fell back to Longcheng and was replaced by Northern Yan in 407.

confidenceNote.zh: 十六國時期疆域只錄關鍵年份，為約略復原。
confidenceNote.en: Borders in the Sixteen Kingdoms period are recorded at key dates only and are approximate.

summary.zh: 羌人姚萇所建，386年入長安。姚興時一度據有關中、河南。417年劉裕北伐，王鎮惡克長安，姚泓出降，國亡。
summary.en: Founded by the Qiang leader Yao Chang, who entered Chang'an in 386. Under Yao Xing it held Guanzhong and the lands south of the Yellow River. In 417 Liu Yu's northern expedition took Chang'an and Yao Hong surrendered.

note.en: after the clan took the surname Yuan

summary.zh: 鮮卑拓跋珪386年即代王位於牛川，同年改稱魏王。398年都平城；太武帝滅夏、北燕、北涼，439年統一北方。孝文帝493年定遷都洛陽之計，推行漢化。六鎮之亂（524）後國勢瓦解，534年分裂為東、西魏。
summary.en: The Tuoba Xianbei leader Tuoba Gui took the title King of Dai at Niuchuan in 386 and changed it to King of Wei the same year. The capital was Pingcheng from 398; Emperor Taiwu destroyed Xia, Northern Yan and Northern Liang and united the north in 439. Emperor Xiaowen resolved in 493 to move the capital to Luoyang and pushed sinicization. After the Six Garrisons revolt (524) the state broke apart, splitting into Eastern and Western Wei in 534.

passages.textZh: 登國元年春正月戊申，帝即代王位，郊天，建元，大會於牛川。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Dengguo, in spring, the first month, on wushen, the Emperor took the title King of Dai, sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar, proclaimed an era and held a great assembly at Niuchuan.

passages.textZh: 夏四月，改稱魏王。
passages.textEn: In summer, the fourth month, he changed his title to King of Wei.

summary.zh: 劉裕受晉禪建宋，都建康。初據有河南、山東；宋文帝元嘉年間屢次北伐，均未能久守。466–469年淮北四州盡失於魏。479年蕭道成代宋建齊。
summary.en: Liu Yu took the Jin abdication and founded Song at Jiankang. At first it held the lands south of the Yellow River and Shandong; Emperor Wen's northern campaigns of the Yuanjia era never held their gains. Between 466 and 469 the four provinces north of the Huai were lost to Wei. Xiao Daocheng replaced Song with Qi in 479.

passages.textZh: 永初元年夏六月丁卯，設壇於南郊，即皇帝位，柴燎告天。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Yongchu, summer, the sixth month, on dingmao, he set up an altar in the southern suburb, took the imperial throne, and burned offerings to announce it to Heaven.

summary.zh: 蕭道成代宋建齊，都建康，國祚二十三年。齊明帝以後宗室相殘，東昏侯失政；501年雍州刺史蕭衍自襄陽起兵，次年代齊建梁。
summary.en: Xiao Daocheng replaced Song with Qi at Jiankang; it lasted twenty-three years. After Emperor Ming the imperial clan turned on itself and the Marquis of Donghun misruled; in 501 Xiao Yan, governor of Yong, rose at Xiangyang and founded Liang the next year.

summary.zh: 蕭衍建梁，都建康，在位四十八年，崇佛，文化鼎盛。547年納東魏叛將侯景，次年侯景反，549年陷臺城，梁武帝憂憤而死。此後江陵、建康相繼易手，557年陳霸先代梁。
summary.en: Xiao Yan founded Liang at Jiankang and reigned forty-eight years; he patronised Buddhism and the court's culture flourished. In 547 he accepted the Eastern Wei defector Hou Jing, who rebelled the next year and took the palace city in 549; the emperor died in grief and anger. Jiangling and Jiankang changed hands in turn, and Chen Baxian replaced Liang in 557.

passages.textZh: 天監元年夏四月丙寅，高祖卽皇帝位於南郊。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Tianjian, summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, Gaozu took the imperial throne in the southern suburb.

summary.zh: 陳霸先代梁建陳，都建康，疆域為南朝最小。陳宣帝太建五年（573）北伐收復淮南，578年呂梁兵敗後復失。589年正月隋軍渡江，陳亡，南北復歸統一。
summary.en: Chen Baxian replaced Liang with Chen at Jiankang — the smallest of the southern states. Emperor Xuan's northern campaign of 573 won back the land between the Huai and the Yangtze, lost again after the defeat at Lüliang in 578. In the first month of 589 the Sui armies crossed the Yangtze; Chen fell and north and south were one again.

passages.textZh: 永定元年冬十月乙亥，高祖即皇帝位于南郊，柴燎告天
passages.textEn: In the first year of Yongding, winter, the tenth month, on yihai, Gaozu took the imperial throne in the southern suburb and burned offerings to announce it to Heaven

summary.zh: 534年北魏孝武帝西奔長安，高歡另立元善見，遷都於鄴，史稱東魏。實權在高氏，550年高洋受禪建北齊。
summary.en: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west to Chang'an in 534, Gao Huan set up Yuan Shanjian and moved the court to Ye: the Eastern Wei. Real power lay with the Gao family; in 550 Gao Yang took the abdication and founded Northern Qi.

passages.textZh: 丙子，車駕北遷于鄴。詔齊獻武王留後部分。改司州為洛州，以衞大將軍、尚書令元弼為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、洛州刺史，鎮洛陽。
passages.textEn: On bingzi the imperial carriage moved north to Ye. The Prince Xianwu of Qi [Gao Huan] was ordered to stay behind and arrange matters. Si Province was renamed Luo Province, and Yuan Bi was made governor of Luo Province, guarding Luoyang.

summary.zh: 孝武帝入關後為宇文泰所殺，宇文泰立元寶炬，都長安，史稱西魏。創府兵制；553年取蜀，554年破江陵。557年宇文覺受禪建北周。
summary.en: Emperor Xiaowu, having gone west, was killed by Yuwen Tai, who set up Yuan Baoju at Chang'an: the Western Wei. It created the garrison-militia (fubing) system, took Sichuan in 553 and sacked Jiangling in 554. In 557 Yuwen Jue took the abdication and founded Northern Zhou.

passages.textZh: 丁未，帝為椿等迫脅，遂出於長安。己酉，齊獻武王入洛，賀拔勝走還荊州。
passages.textEn: On dingwei, the Emperor, coerced by [Husi] Chun and others, left for Chang'an. On jiyou the Prince Xianwu of Qi entered Luoyang, and Heba Sheng fled back to Jing Province.

summary.zh: 高洋代東魏建齊，都鄴，以晉陽為別都。曾大築長城以防柔然、突厥。後主高緯時政治敗壞，577年正月北周武帝攻入鄴城，北齊亡。
summary.en: Gao Yang replaced Eastern Wei with Qi at Ye, with Jinyang as a second capital, and built long walls against the Rouran and the Türks. Under its last ruler Gao Wei government decayed, and in the first month of 577 Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou took Ye.

passages.textZh: 是年，發夫一百八十萬人築長城，自幽州北夏口至恒州九百餘里。
passages.textEn: This year 1,800,000 labourers were called up to build a long wall, more than nine hundred li from Xiakou north of You Province to Heng Province.

summary.zh: 宇文覺受西魏禪建周，都長安。周武帝宇文邕親政後滅北齊（577），統一北方。581年外戚楊堅受禪建隋。
summary.en: Yuwen Jue took the Western Wei abdication and founded Zhou at Chang'an. Emperor Wu, Yuwen Yong, destroyed Northern Qi in 577 and reunited the north. In 581 Yang Jian, the empress's father, took the abdication and founded Sui.

summary.zh: 楊堅受北周禪建隋，都長安。開皇九年（589）正月滅陳，結束近三百年的分裂。
summary.en: Yang Jian took the Northern Zhou abdication and founded Sui at Chang'an. In the first month of 589 it destroyed Chen, ending nearly three centuries of division.

summary.zh: 今山西大同。398年起為北魏都城近百年；雲岡石窟即開鑿於城西。孝文帝遷洛後改為恆州治所。
summary.en: Modern Datong, Shanxi. Capital of Northern Wei for nearly a century from 398; the Yungang caves were cut into the cliffs west of the city. After the move to Luoyang it became the seat of Heng Province.

summary.zh: 今江蘇鎮江，長江下游渡口。永嘉之後北方流民聚居於此，東晉僑置徐州，劉宋改稱南徐州。劉裕即起兵於京口。
summary.en: Modern Zhenjiang, the great crossing of the lower Yangtze. Northern refugees settled here after 311; Eastern Jin set up its émigré Xu Province here, renamed South Xu by Song. Liu Yu rose in arms at Jingkou.

passages.locator: 卷三十五 州郡志一 南徐州
passages.textZh: 南徐州刺史，晉永嘉大亂，幽、冀、青、并、兗州及徐州之淮北流民，相率過淮，亦有過江在晉陵郡界者。
passages.textEn: South Xu Province: in the great disorders of the Yongjia era of Jin, refugees from You, Ji, Qing, Bing and Yan provinces, and from Xu Province north of the Huai, crossed the Huai together, and some crossed the Yangtze and settled within Jinling commandery.

note.en: name in the Eastern Jin and southern histories

summary.zh: 淮南重鎮（今安徽壽縣），南北必爭之地。南朝史書多作「壽陽」，《魏書》作「壽春」。500年裴叔業以城降魏，526年梁復取，549年入東魏，573年陳克之，579年入北周。
summary.en: The great fortress of Huainan (modern Shou County, Anhui), fought over by north and south. The southern histories mostly call it Shouyang, the Book of Wei Shouchun. Pei Shuye surrendered it to Wei in 500; Liang retook it in 526; it went to Eastern Wei in 549, to Chen in 573 and to Northern Zhou in 579.

passages.textZh: 丁未，蕭寶卷豫州刺史裴叔業以壽春內屬，驃騎大將軍、彭城王勰帥車騎十萬赴之。
passages.textEn: On dingwei, Pei Shuye, governor of Yu Province for Xiao Baojuan [the Qi ruler], submitted with Shouchun; Xie, Prince of Pengcheng, went to take it over with a hundred thousand chariots and horse.

summary.zh: 在今山東青州西北，南燕都城。410年劉裕攻克後毀之，青州改治東陽城。
summary.en: North-west of modern Qingzhou, Shandong; capital of Southern Yan. Liu Yu took it in 410 and razed it, and the provincial seat moved to Dongyang.

summary.zh: 夏國赫連勃勃所築都城（今陝西靖邊白城子），城以白色三合土夯築，至今猶存。427年北魏太武帝攻克。
summary.en: Capital built by Helian Bobo of Xia (modern Baichengzi, Jingbian, Shaanxi), its walls rammed from white lime-earth that still stands. Emperor Taiwu of Wei took it in 427.

summary.zh: 淮河南岸重鎮（今安徽鳳陽東北）。507年梁軍在此大破北魏中山王元英。
summary.en: Fortress on the south bank of the Huai (north-east of modern Fengyang, Anhui). Here in 507 the Liang armies routed the Wei army of Yuan Ying, Prince of Zhongshan.

summary.zh: 淮河南岸城邑。451年臧質堅守盱眙，北魏太武帝攻之月餘不下。
summary.en: Town on the south bank of the Huai. In 451 Zang Zhi held it against Emperor Taiwu of Wei for over a month.

summary.zh: 今江蘇徐州，徐州治所，南北要衝。466年宋徐州刺史薛安都以城降魏，此後屬北朝。
summary.en: Modern Xuzhou, seat of Xu Province and a crossroads between north and south. In 466 the Song governor Xue Andu surrendered it to Wei; from then on it was northern.

summary.zh: 今山西太原，并州治所。東魏、北齊時高氏霸府所在，為北齊別都。
summary.en: Modern Taiyuan, seat of Bing Province. The Gao family ran Eastern Wei and Northern Qi from here; it was Northern Qi's second capital.

summary.zh: 西魏所築城（今山西稷山西南），扼汾水下游。542、546年高歡兩次圍攻，皆不克。
summary.en: Fort built by Western Wei (south-west of modern Jishan, Shanxi), commanding the lower Fen. Gao Huan besieged it in 542 and 546 and failed both times.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年不詳。
confidenceNote.en: Year of birth unknown.

summary.zh: 匈奴屠各部貴族，字元海。304年以漢室外甥自居，於左國城稱漢王，後徙平陽、稱帝，開十六國之局。
summary.en: A noble of the Xiongnu Chuge tribe, courtesy name Yuanhai. In 304, claiming kinship with the Han royal house, he took the title King of Han at Zuoguocheng; he later moved to Pingyang and took the imperial title, opening the age of the Sixteen Kingdoms.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零一 劉元海載記
passages.textZh: 吾又漢氏之甥，約為兄弟，兄亡弟紹，不亦可乎？且可稱漢，追尊後主，以懷人望。
passages.textEn: "I am, besides, a nephew of the house of Han, bound to it as a brother; when the elder brother dies the younger carries on — is that not fitting? Let us call ourselves Han and posthumously honour the Later Sovereign, to win men's hopes."

summary.zh: 琅邪王氏，輔佐司馬睿在江東立國，歷仕元、明、成三帝。新亭對泣時勸眾人「克復神州」。時人以「王與馬，共天下」形容王氏與晉室的關係。
summary.en: Of the Wang clan of Langye, he helped Sima Rui build the state east of the Yangtze and served three emperors. At the Xinting gathering he told the weeping exiles to "win back the Divine Land". People said of the Wang clan and the throne: "the Wang and the Ma share the realm".

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 過江人士，每至暇日，相要出新亭飲宴。周顗中坐而歎曰：「風景不殊，舉目有江河之異。」皆相視流涕。惟導愀然變色曰：「當共戮力王室，克復神州，何至作楚囚相對泣邪！」眾收淚而謝之。
passages.textEn: The gentlemen who had crossed the river would meet at Xinting on their days of leisure to drink and feast. Zhou Yi, seated among them, sighed: "The scenery is no different — but lift your eyes and there is the difference between the Jiang and the He." They looked at one another and wept. Only Wang Dao's face changed and he said sternly: "We should be joining our strength for the royal house to win back the Divine Land — why come to this, weeping at one another like prisoners of Chu?" They dried their tears and apologised.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 帝初鎮江東，威名未著，敦與從弟導等同心翼戴，以隆中興，時人為之語曰：「王與馬，共天下。」
passages.textEn: When the emperor first took charge east of the Yangtze his name carried little weight. Wang Dun, his cousin Wang Dao and others supported him with one heart to raise up the restoration, and people of the day had a saying for it: "The Wang and the Ma share the realm."

question.zh: 周顗在新亭說的是「江河之異」還是「山河之異」？
question.en: At Xinting, did Zhou Yi speak of the difference of "rivers" or of "mountains and rivers"?

claim.zh: 「舉目有江河之異」：放眼望去，是長江而非黃河。
claim.en: "Lift your eyes and there is the difference between the Jiang and the He" — the Yangtze, not the Yellow River.

source.en: Book of Jin, Wang Dao (compiled in the Tang)

accounts.quoteZh: 風景不殊，舉目有江河之異。

claim.zh: 「正自有山河之異」：山河已不是原來的山河。
claim.en: "Yet the mountains and rivers are different" — the land itself is not the same.

source.en: Shishuo xinyu, Speech and conversation (Liu Song)

accounts.quoteZh: 中坐而嘆曰：「風景不殊，正自有山河之異。」

note.zh: 《世說新語》早於《晉書》約兩百年，《晉書》此段多採其文而有改動。
note.en: The Shishuo xinyu is some two centuries older than the Book of Jin, which took much of this passage from it with changes.

summary.zh: 范陽人，率宗族流民南渡。313年受命為豫州刺史北伐，渡江時擊楫中流而誓。一度收復黃河以南大片土地，321年病卒於雍丘。
summary.en: From Fanyang, he brought his clan and followers south. Appointed governor of Yu Province in 313 to march north, he struck his oar in midstream and swore an oath. He won back much of the land south of the Yellow River before dying of illness at Yongqiu in 321.

label.zh: 自京口渡江北伐，中流擊楫
label.en: Crosses the Yangtze from Jingkou; the oath in midstream
Recovers Qiao and the surrounding lands

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 仍將本流徙部曲百餘家渡江，中流擊楫而誓曰：「祖逖不能清中原而復濟者，有如大江！」辭色壯烈，眾皆慨歎。屯于江陰，起冶鑄兵器，得二千餘人而後進。
passages.textEn: Taking the hundred-odd households of his refugee following, he crossed the Yangtze. In midstream he struck the oar and swore: "If I, Zu Ti, cannot clear the Central Plain and yet cross back over, let it be as this great river!" His words and bearing were fierce and all who heard him sighed. He camped at Jiangyin, set up forges to cast weapons, and moved on once he had over two thousand men.

summary.zh: 陳郡謝氏，隱居東山多年後出仕，官至宰相。383年前秦大舉南侵，他坐鎮建康，以侄謝玄等迎戰，淝水大捷傳來時正與客對弈。
summary.en: Of the Xie clan of Chen commandery; after years in retirement at Dongshan he took office and rose to chief minister. When Former Qin invaded in 383 he directed the defence from Jiankang, sending his nephew Xie Xuan and others to meet it; the news of the Fei River victory reached him over a game of weiqi.

label.en: In Jiankang when the news of the Fei River arrives

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 玄等既破堅，有驛書至，安方對客圍棋，看書既竟，便攝放床上，了無喜色，棋如故。客問之，徐答云：「小兒輩遂已破賊。」既罷，還內，過戶限，心喜甚，不覺屐齒之折，其矯情鎮物如此。
passages.textEn: When Xie Xuan and the others had broken Fu Jian, a courier's letter arrived while Xie An was playing weiqi with a guest. He read it through, put it down on the couch, showed not a trace of joy and played on as before. When the guest asked, he answered slowly: "The boys have beaten the enemy after all." When the game was over and he went back inside, he was so overjoyed that, stepping over the threshold, he did not notice he had broken the tooth of his clog. Such was his self-command.

summary.zh: 前秦天王，氐人。任用王猛，統一北方。383年不聽群臣勸阻大舉南伐，敗於淝水，北方隨即分崩，385年為姚萇所殺。
summary.en: Heavenly King of Former Qin, a Di. With Wang Meng as minister he united the north. In 383, against his ministers' advice, he launched a great invasion of the south and was routed at the Fei River; the north fell apart and Yao Chang killed him in 385.

label.en: Camps at Shouyang, facing the Fei

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十四 苻堅載記下
passages.textZh: 以吾之眾旅，投鞭于江，足斷其流。
passages.textEn: "With my host, if every man threw his whip into the river it would be enough to stop its flow."

summary.zh: 北魏道武帝。386年即代王位於牛川，同年改稱魏王；擊破後燕，取并州、中山與鄴，398年定都平城。
summary.en: Emperor Daowu of Northern Wei. He took the title King of Dai at Niuchuan in 386 and changed it to King of Wei the same year; he broke Later Yan, took Bing Province, Zhongshan and Ye, and made Pingcheng his capital in 398.

label.en: Takes the title King of Dai at Niuchuan
Killed by his son Tuoba Shao

passages.textZh: 登國元年春正月戊申，帝即代王位，郊天，建元，大會於牛川。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Dengguo, spring, the first month, on wushen, the Emperor took the title King of Dai, sacrificed to Heaven, proclaimed an era and held a great assembly at Niuchuan.

summary.zh: 宋武帝，出身京口寒微之家，以北府兵起家。404年起兵討桓玄；409–410年滅南燕，416–417年北伐滅後秦，收復洛陽、長安。420年受晉禪建宋。
summary.en: Emperor Wu of Song, from a poor family of Jingkou, who rose through the Beifu army. He rose against Huan Xuan in 404, destroyed Southern Yan in 409–410, and in 416–417 marched north, destroyed Later Qin and took back Luoyang and Chang'an. In 420 he took the Jin abdication and founded Song.

label.en: Rises against Huan Xuan at Jingkou
The fleet leaves the capital against Southern Yan
At Xiapi, leaves the ships and marches on
Takes the throne in the southern suburb of Jiankang

passages.textZh: 三月，公抗表北討，以丹陽尹孟昶監中軍留府事。四月，舟師發京都，泝淮入泗。五月，至下邳，留船艦輜重，步軍進琅邪。
passages.textEn: In the third month the Duke memorialised and marched north, leaving Meng Chang, Intendant of Danyang, in charge at home. In the fourth month the fleet left the capital, went up the Huai and into the Si. In the fifth month he reached Xiapi, left his ships and baggage, and advanced on foot into Langye.

passages.textZh: 七月，至陝城。龍驤將軍王鎮惡伐木為舟，自河浮渭。八月，扶風太守沈田子大破姚泓於藍田。王鎮惡剋長安，生擒泓。九月，公至長安。長安豐全，帑藏盈積。
passages.textEn: In the seventh month he reached Shan. The general Wang Zhen'e cut timber for boats and floated from the Yellow River into the Wei. In the eighth month Shen Tianzi, Governor of Fufeng, routed Yao Hong at Lantian; Wang Zhen'e took Chang'an and captured Yao Hong alive. In the ninth month the Duke reached Chang'an. The city was intact and its treasuries full.

passages.textZh: 永初元年夏六月丁卯，設壇於南郊，即皇帝位，柴燎告天。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Yongchu, summer, the sixth month, on dingmao, he set up an altar in the southern suburb, took the imperial throne and burned offerings to announce it to Heaven.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年不詳。
confidenceNote.en: Year of birth unknown.

summary.zh: 劉宋名將，隨劉裕北伐為前鋒；431年率軍救滑臺，轉戰至歷城，因糧盡而還。436年宋文帝猜忌，將其收捕誅殺。
summary.en: A leading Song general who led the vanguard on Liu Yu's northern expedition. In 431 he marched to relieve Huatai and fought his way to Licheng before running out of grain and turning back. In 436 Emperor Wen, fearing him, had him arrested and executed.

label.en: Vanguard of the northern expedition at Tong Pass
Fights his way to Licheng, turns back for want of grain

passages.locator: 卷四十三 檀道濟傳
passages.textZh: 初，道濟見收，脫幘投地曰：「乃復壞汝萬里之長城！」
passages.textEn: When he was arrested, Tan Daoji tore off his headcloth, threw it down and said: "So you tear down your own Great Wall of ten thousand li!"

question.en: Did he really "count sand as grain"?

claim.zh: 有：糧盡時夜間唱籌量沙，上覆少量米，使魏軍以為糧多而不敢追。
claim.en: Yes: with the grain gone, he had sand measured out at night with the tallies called aloud and a little rice spread over it, so the Wei army thought he had plenty and dared not pursue.

source.en: History of the Southern Dynasties, Tan Daoji (Li Yanshou, Tang)

accounts.quoteZh: 道濟夜唱籌量沙，以所余少米散其上。及旦，魏軍謂資糧有餘，故不復追，以降者妄，斬以徇。

claim.zh: 本傳不載此事。
claim.en: His biography in the Book of Song does not mention it.

source.en: Book of Song, Tan Daoji (Shen Yue, Liang)

note.zh: 此事最早見於後出的《南史》，較宋書晚一百七十年，可能出自軼聞。
note.en: The story first appears in the later History of the Southern Dynasties, some 170 years after the Book of Song, and may come from anecdote.

note.zh: 小字；南朝童謠稱「佛狸死卯年」
note.en: childhood name; a southern rhyme said "Foli dies in a mao year"

summary.zh: 北魏太武帝，小字佛狸。427年克夏都統萬，436年滅北燕，439年滅北涼，統一北方。450年大舉南侵至長江北岸瓜步，次年北返。452年為宦官宗愛所弒。
summary.en: Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei, childhood name Foli. He took the Xia capital Tongwan in 427, destroyed Northern Yan in 436 and Northern Liang in 439, uniting the north. In 450 he invaded the south as far as Guabu on the north bank of the Yangtze, turning back the next year. The eunuch Zong Ai murdered him in 452.

label.en: Reaches the Yangtze; a camp-palace on Mount Guabu

passages.textZh: 九月丙戌，牧犍兄子萬年率麾下來降。是日，牧犍與左右文武五千人面縛軍門，帝解其縛，待以藩臣之禮。收其城內戶口二十餘萬，倉庫珍寶不可稱計。
passages.textEn: In the ninth month, on bingxu, Mujian's nephew Wannian came over with his men. That day Mujian and five thousand of his officials and officers came to the camp gate with their hands bound; the Emperor untied them and treated him with the courtesy due to a vassal. Over two hundred thousand people in the city were registered, and the treasures in its storehouses were past counting.

passages.textZh: 三月甲寅，帝崩於永安宮，時年四十五。祕不發喪，中常侍宗愛矯皇后令，殺東平王翰，迎南安王余入而立之
passages.textEn: In the third month, on jiayin, the Emperor died in the Yong'an Palace, aged forty-five. The death was kept secret; the eunuch Zong Ai forged an order of the empress, killed Han, Prince of Dongping, and brought in Yu, Prince of Nan'an, and set him on the throne

summary.zh: 北魏孝文帝，本姓拓跋，後改姓元。493年借南伐之名率軍至洛陽，群臣請停南伐，遂定遷都之計；494年遷洛，推行改服、改姓等漢化措施。499年病逝於南征途中。
summary.en: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei, born a Tuoba, who changed the clan name to Yuan. In 493 he led his army to Luoyang under the pretext of a southern campaign; when his ministers begged him to stop, he settled on moving the capital instead. He moved to Luoyang in 494 and imposed Chinese dress, surnames and customs. He died on campaign in the south in 499.

label.zh: 至洛陽，群臣請停南伐，定遷都之計
label.en: At Luoyang; asked to stop the campaign, he settles on moving the capital

label.zh: 設壇於滑臺城東，告遷都之意
label.en: At an altar east of Huatai, announces the move
Moves into the new palace at Ye
Dies at the travelling palace on the Gutang plain

passages.textZh: 丁丑，戎服執鞭，御馬而出，羣臣稽顙於馬前，請停南伐，帝乃止。仍定遷都之計。
passages.textEn: On dingchou, in armour and holding a whip, he rode out; the ministers knocked their heads on the ground before his horse and begged him to call off the southern campaign, and he stopped. So the plan to move the capital was settled.

passages.textZh: 夏四月丙午朔，帝崩于穀塘原之行宮，時年三十三。
passages.textEn: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day, bingwu, the Emperor died at the travelling palace on the Gutang plain, aged thirty-three.

summary.zh: 梁武帝。原為南齊雍州刺史，501年自襄陽起兵，次年代齊建梁。在位四十八年，篤信佛教，數度捨身同泰寺。晚年納侯景，致侯景之亂，臺城陷後憂憤而死。
summary.en: Emperor Wu of Liang. Governor of Yong Province under Southern Qi, he rose at Xiangyang in 501 and founded Liang the next year. He reigned forty-eight years, a devout Buddhist who several times gave himself to the Tongtai monastery. In old age he took in Hou Jing, whose rebellion followed; after the palace city fell he died in grief and anger.

label.en: Governor of Yong Province at Xiangyang
Takes the throne in the southern suburb

passages.textZh: 我家國猶若金甌，無一傷缺，今便受地，詎是事宜，脫致紛紜，非可悔也。
passages.textEn: "My realm is like a golden bowl, without a crack or a chip. To accept territory now — is that the right thing? If it brings trouble, it will be past regretting."

passages.textZh: 三月庚子，高祖幸同泰寺，設無遮大會，捨身……
passages.textEn: In the third month, on gengzi, Gaozu went to the Tongtai monastery, held a great assembly open to all, and gave himself [to the monastery]…

passages.textZh: 五月丙辰，高祖崩于淨居殿，時年八十六。
passages.textEn: In the fifth month, on bingchen, Gaozu died in the Jingju Hall, aged eighty-six.

summary.zh: 梁名將。506年克合肥；507年率豫州軍馳援鍾離，與曹景宗合力大破北魏中山王元英。
summary.en: A Liang general. He took Hefei in 506, and in 507 hurried the Yu Province army to relieve Zhongli, where with Cao Jingzong he routed the Wei army of Yuan Ying.

label.zh: 大破魏軍於鍾離邵陽洲
label.en: Routs the Wei army at Shaoyang island, Zhongli

passages.textZh: 叡曰：「鐘離今鑿穴而處，負戶而汲，車馳卒奔，猶恐其後，而況緩乎！魏人已墮吾腹中，卿曹勿憂也。」旬日而至邵陽。
passages.textEn: Wei Rui said: "Zhongli is living in holes it has dug, fetching water under shields made of doors. Even racing our carts and running our men we may be too late — how can we go slowly? The Wei army has already fallen into our belly; do not worry, gentlemen." In ten days he reached Shaoyang.

summary.zh: 梁將。528年奉命護送北魏降王元顥北還，率白袍軍自銍縣轉戰至洛陽，十四旬間平三十二城，四十七戰。元顥失敗後南歸。
summary.en: A Liang general. In 528 he was sent to escort the Wei prince Yuan Hao home; his white-robed army fought its way from Zhi county to Luoyang, taking thirty-two cities in a hundred and forty days, in forty-seven battles. When Yuan Hao fell he came back south.

label.en: Sent to escort Yuan Hao north

passages.locator: 卷三十二 陳慶之傳
passages.textZh: 慶之麾下悉著白袍，所向披靡。先是洛陽童謠曰：「名師大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍。」自發銍縣至於洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。
passages.textEn: Qingzhi's men all wore white robes, and everything gave way before them. Before this a children's rhyme in Luoyang went: "Famous generals and great commanders, do not trust your walls — a thousand troops and ten thousand horse make way for the White Robes." From leaving Zhi county to reaching Luoyang, in fourteen ten-day periods they took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles, and nothing stood in their way.

passages.textZh: 冬十月丁亥，以魏北海王元顥爲魏主，遣東宮直閤將軍陳慶之衛送還北。
passages.textEn: In winter, the tenth month, on dinghai, Yuan Hao, the Wei Prince of Beihai, was made ruler of Wei, and Chen Qingzhi, general of the Eastern Palace, was sent to escort him north.

confidenceNote.zh: 河陰遇害人數，諸書所記不一（二千餘人之說見於後世通行敘述）。
confidenceNote.en: The number killed at Heyin differs between sources.

summary.zh: 契胡酋長，鎮秀容。528年孝明帝暴崩，爾朱榮舉兵入洛，立孝莊帝，於河陰沉殺胡太后與幼主，並屠戮王公百官。530年為孝莊帝誘殺。
summary.en: Chieftain of the Qihu at Xiurong. In 528, after Emperor Xiaoming's sudden death, he marched on Luoyang, enthroned Emperor Xiaozhuang, drowned the empress dowager and the child emperor at Heyin and massacred the court. Emperor Xiaozhuang lured him in and killed him in 530.

note.en: posthumous title given by Northern Qi

summary.zh: 鮮卑化的漢人，懷朔鎮出身。532年擊滅爾朱氏，掌北魏朝政；534年孝武帝西奔後另立孝靜帝，遷都鄴，實為東魏之主。屢與宇文泰交戰，546年圍玉壁不克，次年病卒。
summary.en: A Chinese brought up among the Xianbei of the Huaishuo garrison. In 532 he destroyed the Erzhu clan and took control of the Wei court; when Emperor Xiaowu fled west in 534 he set up Emperor Xiaojing at Ye and was in effect master of Eastern Wei. He fought Yuwen Tai again and again, failed before Yubi in 546 and died the next year.

note.en: posthumous title given by Northern Zhou

summary.zh: 鮮卑宇文部人，武川鎮出身。迎北魏孝武帝入關，後另立文帝，掌西魏政權。537年以少勝多大破高歡於沙苑；創立府兵制。
summary.en: Of the Yuwen Xianbei, from the Wuchuan garrison. He received Emperor Xiaowu in Guanzhong, later set up Emperor Wen, and ran the Western Wei. In 537 he routed Gao Huan's far larger army at Shayuan; he founded the fubing militia system.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.textZh: 冬十月壬辰，至沙苑，距齊神武軍六十餘里。齊神武聞太祖至，引軍來會。癸巳旦，候騎告齊神武軍且至。太祖召諸將謀之。李弼曰：「彼眾我寡，不可平地置陣。此東十里有渭曲，可先據以待之。」
passages.textEn: In winter, the tenth month, on renchen, he reached Shayuan, sixty li from the army of Shenwu of Qi [Gao Huan]. Hearing that Taizu had come, Shenwu brought his army to meet him. At dawn on guisi the scouts reported that Shenwu's army was near. Taizu called his generals to council. Li Bi said: "They are many and we are few; we cannot draw up on open ground. Ten li east of here is the bend of the Wei — let us take it first and wait for them."

summary.zh: 羯人（一說鮮卑化），東魏大將，專制河南。547年高歡死後以河南十三州降梁，旋為東魏所敗，退據壽陽；548年舉兵反梁，次年攻陷臺城，551年自立為帝，國號漢。552年兵敗被殺。
summary.en: An Eastern Wei general of Jie (or Xianbei) origin who ruled Henan. When Gao Huan died in 547 he went over to Liang with thirteen provinces, was quickly beaten by Eastern Wei and fell back to Shouyang. In 548 he rebelled against Liang, took the palace city the next year, made himself emperor of "Han" in 551, and was beaten and killed in 552.

label.en: Goes over to Liang with thirteen provinces

passages.textZh: 景軍食盡，士卒並北人，不樂南渡，其將暴顯等各率所部降於紹宗。景軍潰散，乃與腹心數騎自峽石濟淮……
passages.textEn: Jing's army ran out of food; his men were all northerners who had no wish to go south, and his officers Bao Xian and others went over to [Murong] Shaozong with their troops. Jing's army broke up, and with a few trusted riders he crossed the Huai at Xiashi…

summary.zh: 陳武帝，吳興人。起自嶺南，侯景之亂中與王僧辯共平侯景；555年襲殺王僧辯，557年代梁建陳。
summary.en: Emperor Wu of Chen, from Wuxing. He rose in the far south, and in the Hou Jing rebellion joined Wang Sengbian to put it down; in 555 he killed Wang Sengbian in a surprise attack, and in 557 replaced Liang with Chen.

label.en: Comes north from Lingnan against Hou Jing

summary.zh: 梁朝文學侍從，侯景之亂時奔江陵。554年出使西魏，適逢江陵陷落，遂被留長安，歷仕西魏、北周，晚年作《哀江南賦》寄託鄉關之思。
summary.en: A literary courtier of Liang who fled to Jiangling during the Hou Jing rebellion. Sent as envoy to Western Wei in 554, he was in Chang'an when Jiangling fell and was kept there, serving Western Wei and Northern Zhou; late in life he wrote the "Lament for the South" out of longing for home.

label.zh: 出使西魏，江陵陷後留長安
label.en: Envoy to Western Wei; kept in Chang'an after Jiangling falls

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.textZh: 粵以戊辰之年，建亥之月，大盜移國，金陵瓦解。余乃竄身荒谷，公私塗炭。華陽奔命，有去無歸，中興道消，窮於甲戌。三日哭於都亭，三年囚於別館。
passages.textEn: In the year wuchen [548], in the month jianhai [the tenth], a great bandit stole the realm and Jinling fell to pieces. I fled into wild valleys; public and private alike were in mud and ashes. I ran to serve at Huayang and went never to return; the restoration faded and came to its end in jiaxu [554]. Three days I wept at the city pavilion, three years I was a prisoner in the guest lodge.

confidenceNote.zh: 卒年約在開皇年間，確年不詳。
confidenceNote.en: He died in the Kaihuang era; the exact year is not known.

summary.zh: 琅邪顏氏，仕梁元帝於江陵；554年江陵陷落被俘入西魏，後冒險奔北齊；577年齊亡入周，入隋後為太子學士。一生「三為亡國之人」，著《顏氏家訓》。
summary.en: Of the Yan clan of Langye. He served Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jiangling; captured when Jiangling fell in 554, he was taken to Western Wei, then risked escape to Northern Qi; when Qi fell in 577 he passed to Zhou, and under Sui he served the crown prince. Three times his state fell under him. He wrote the Family Instructions of the Yan Clan.

label.en: Serves Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jiangling
Captured at Jiangling and taken west
Passes to Zhou when Qi falls
Under Sui, scholar to the crown prince

passages.locator: 卷四十五 文苑傳 顏之推
passages.textZh: 齊亡入周，大象末為御史上士。隋開皇中，太子召為學士，甚見禮重。尋以疾終。有文三十卷，撰《家訓》二十篇，並行於世。
passages.textEn: When Qi fell he passed to Zhou, and at the end of the Daxiang era was a senior censor. In the Kaihuang era of Sui the crown prince summoned him as a scholar and treated him with great honour. Soon afterwards he died of illness. He left writings in thirty juan and the Family Instructions in twenty chapters, all still read.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年不詳。
confidenceNote.en: Year of birth unknown.

summary.zh: 北魏地理學家、官員，為《水經》作注四十卷，記述千餘條水道及沿岸地理、古蹟。執法嚴峻，527年出使關中，為蕭寶夤所害於陰盤驛亭。
summary.en: A Northern Wei official and geographer who wrote a forty-juan commentary on the Classic of Waterways, describing over a thousand rivers and the places along them. A severe magistrate, he was sent to Guanzhong in 527 and killed by Xiao Baoyin at the Yinpan post station.

label.en: Killed at the Yinpan post station

passages.locator: 卷八十九 酷吏傳 酈道元
passages.textZh: 是時雍州刺史蕭寶夤反狀稍露，悅等諷朝廷遣為關右大使，遂為寶夤所害，死於陰盤驛亭。 道元好學，歷覽奇書。撰注水經四十卷、本志十三篇，又為七聘及諸文，皆行於世。
passages.textEn: At this time signs of rebellion were appearing in Xiao Baoyin, governor of Yong Province, and Yue and others prompted the court to send Daoyuan as envoy to the lands west of the passes, where Baoyin had him killed; he died at the Yinpan post station. Daoyuan loved learning and read widely in rare books. He wrote a commentary on the Classic of Waterways in forty juan, a treatise in thirteen chapters, the Seven Invitations and other writings, all of which circulate.

summary.zh: 北齊宗室，封蘭陵王。564年邙山之戰率五百騎衝入周軍，解金墉之圍，將士歌之為《蘭陵王入陣曲》。573年為後主所忌，賜死。
summary.en: A Northern Qi prince, Prince of Lanling. At Mangshan in 564 he charged into the Zhou army with five hundred horsemen and broke the siege of Jinyong; his soldiers made a song of it, the "Prince of Lanling Goes into Battle". The last Qi ruler, fearing him, ordered him to die in 573.

label.en: Breaks the siege of Jinyong in the battle of Mangshan

passages.locator: 卷十一 文襄六王傳
passages.textZh: 芒山之敗，長恭為中軍，率五百騎再入周軍，遂至金墉之下，被圍甚急，城上人弗識，長恭免冑示之面，乃下弩手救之，於是大捷。武士共歌謠之，為蘭陵王入陣曲是也。
passages.textEn: At the Mangshan crisis Changgong commanded the centre and twice charged into the Zhou army with five hundred horse, reaching the foot of Jinyong. The city was hard pressed; the men on the walls did not recognise him until he took off his helmet and showed his face, and then they sent down crossbowmen to help him, and it became a great victory. The soldiers made a song of it — this is the "Prince of Lanling Goes into Battle".

fiction.zh: 「戴面具上陣」之說出自唐代《教坊記》等後世記載，《北齊書》本傳只記他「免冑示之面」。
fiction.en: The story that he fought in a mask comes from later Tang works such as the Jiaofang ji; his biography in the Book of Northern Qi says only that he "took off his helmet and showed his face".

summary.zh: 北周武帝。572年誅宇文護親政，整頓府兵，禁斷佛道二教。576年東伐北齊，577年正月入鄴，統一北方。次年北伐突厥途中病逝。
summary.en: Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou. He killed the regent Yuwen Hu in 572 and ruled in person, reorganised the militia and banned both Buddhism and Daoism. He marched on Northern Qi in 576 and entered Ye in the first month of 577, uniting the north. He died the next year on campaign against the Türks.

summary.zh: 隋文帝。北周外戚，580年周宣帝死後輔政，平定尉遲迥等起兵；581年受禪建隋。589年遣晉王楊廣等渡江滅陳，統一天下。
summary.en: Emperor Wen of Sui. Father of the Northern Zhou empress, he took the regency when Emperor Xuan died in 580 and crushed the risings of Yuchi Jiong and others; in 581 he took the abdication and founded Sui. In 589 he sent his son Yang Guang and others across the Yangtze to destroy Chen and reunite the empire.

summary.zh: 陳後主，好詩文宴樂。589年正月隋軍渡江，韓擒虎入建康，後主被俘，陳亡。
summary.en: The last ruler of Chen, fond of poetry and feasting. In the first month of 589 the Sui armies crossed the Yangtze; Han Qinhu entered Jiankang, the ruler was captured and Chen fell.

fiction.zh: 後主與張麗華等藏身景陽宮井（後世稱「胭脂井」）被俘之說流傳甚廣，見於《南史》等，本條未錄原文核對。
fiction.en: The famous story that he hid in a well of the Jingyang palace with Zhang Lihua and others (the later "Rouge Well") is widely told, e.g. in the History of the Southern Dynasties; it has not been checked against the text here.

summary.zh: 永嘉五年六月，漢趙劉曜、王彌等攻陷洛陽，焚燒宮廟，殺王公百官士庶三萬餘人，俘晉懷帝至平陽。五年後長安亦陷，西晉亡。北方士民大舉南渡。
summary.en: In the sixth month of 311 the Han-Zhao armies of Liu Yao, Wang Mi and others took Luoyang, burned the palaces and temples, killed over thirty thousand officials and commoners and carried Emperor Huai off to Pingyang. Chang'an fell five years later and the Western Jin ended. People from the north fled south in great numbers.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 曜等遂焚燒宮廟，逼辱妃后，吳王晏、竟陵王楙、尚書左僕射和郁、右僕射曹馥、尚書閭丘沖、袁粲、王緄、河南尹劉默等皆遇害，百官士庶死者三萬餘人。帝蒙塵于平陽，劉聰以帝爲會稽公。
passages.textEn: Liu Yao and the others burned the palaces and ancestral temples and violated the empresses and consorts. Yan, Prince of Wu; Mao, Prince of Jingling; the Vice-Directors He Yu and Cao Fu; the Secretaries Lüqiu Chong, Yuan Can and Wang Gun; the Intendant of Henan Liu Mo and others were all killed, and over thirty thousand officials and commoners died. The emperor was carried off to Pingyang, where Liu Cong made him Duke of Kuaiji.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 十一月乙末，使侍中宋敞送箋于曜，帝乘羊車，肉袒銜壁，輿櫬出降。羣臣號泣攀車，執帝之手，帝亦悲不自勝。
passages.textEn: In the eleventh month, on yiwei [316], he sent the palace attendant Song Chang with a letter to Liu Yao. The emperor rode out in a goat cart, bare to the waist with a jade disc in his mouth and a coffin carried behind, and surrendered. His ministers wailed and clung to the cart, holding his hands; nor could the emperor master his own grief.

confidenceNote.zh: 遷徙歷時數十年，此處以京口為標記；圖上路線為示意，依《宋書·州郡志》所記僑州郡與今人研究（譚其驤《晉永嘉喪亂後之民族遷徙》，1934）。
confidenceNote.en: The movement went on for decades; the marker sits at Jingkou. The routes drawn are schematic, following the émigré provinces recorded in the Song treatise on administrative geography and modern study (Tan Qixiang 1934).

summary.zh: 西晉末年戰亂，北方士族與流民成批渡淮、渡江南下，聚居於京口、晉陵、廣陵、襄陽等地。東晉在其聚居處設立以北方州郡命名的僑州、僑郡、僑縣，如南徐州、南兗州、雍州，以安置流民。人口與文化重心自此南移。
summary.en: In the wars at the end of Western Jin, northern gentry and refugees crossed the Huai and the Yangtze in waves, settling around Jingkou, Jinling, Guangling and Xiangyang. Eastern Jin set up "émigré" provinces, commanderies and counties named after the northern ones they had fled — South Xu, South Yan, Yong — to administer them. The centre of population and culture began to move south.

label.zh: 徐兗流民過淮至京口、晉陵
label.en: From Xu and Yan across the Huai to Jingkou

label.zh: 雍秦流民出樊、沔至襄陽
label.en: From Yong and Qin to Xiangyang

passages.locator: 卷三十五 州郡志一 南徐州
passages.textZh: 南徐州刺史，晉永嘉大亂，幽、冀、青、并、兗州及徐州之淮北流民，相率過淮，亦有過江在晉陵郡界者。晉成帝咸和四年，司空郗鑒又徙流民之在淮南者於晉陵諸縣，其徙過江南及留在江北者，並立僑郡縣以司牧之。
passages.textEn: South Xu Province: in the great disorders of the Yongjia era of Jin, refugees from You, Ji, Qing, Bing and Yan provinces, and from Xu north of the Huai, crossed the Huai together, and some crossed the Yangtze and settled within Jinling commandery. In the fourth year of Xianhe [329] the Minister of Works Xi Jian moved the refugees who were south of the Huai into the counties of Jinling; for those who had crossed to the south and those who stayed north of the river alike, émigré commanderies and counties were set up to govern them.

passages.locator: 卷三十五 州郡志一 南兗州
passages.textZh: 南兗州刺史，中原亂，北州流民多南渡，晉成帝立南兗州，寄治京口。
passages.textEn: South Yan Province: when the Central Plain fell into disorder, many refugees of the northern provinces came south, and Emperor Cheng of Jin set up South Yan Province, lodged at Jingkou.

passages.locator: 卷三十六 州郡志二 青州
passages.textZh: 明帝失淮北，於鬱洲僑立青州，立齊、北海、西海郡。
passages.textEn: When Emperor Ming lost the land north of the Huai, an émigré Qing Province was set up on Yuzhou island, with the commanderies of Qi, Beihai and Xihai.

confidenceNote.zh: 交戰處在壽陽附近的淝（肥）水岸邊，確切地點不詳。月份諸書記為冬季，本圖未錄原文核對，故只標年份。
confidenceNote.en: The fighting was on the Fei near Shouyang; the exact spot is unknown. The month is not given here, as it has not been checked against the text.

summary.zh: 太元八年，前秦苻堅傾國南伐，前鋒苻融攻陷壽陽。東晉以謝石、謝玄等率北府兵迎戰，劉牢之先破秦軍於洛澗；兩軍隔淝水對陣，秦軍後撤時陣腳大亂，苻融戰死，全軍潰敗。前秦隨之瓦解，南北分立之局延續。
summary.en: In 383 Fu Jian of Former Qin threw his whole state into an invasion of the south; his vanguard under Fu Rong took Shouyang. Eastern Jin sent Xie Shi, Xie Xuan and the Beifu army; Liu Laozhi first broke a Qin force at Luojian. The two armies faced each other across the Fei; when the Qin army drew back to let the Jin cross, its lines dissolved, Fu Rong was killed and the whole host fled. Former Qin fell apart, and the division between north and south held.

label.en: Xie Shi and Xie Xuan advance

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十四 苻堅載記下
passages.textZh: 堅發長安，戎卒六十餘萬，騎二十七萬，前後千里，旗鼓相望。
passages.textEn: Fu Jian set out from Chang'an with over six hundred thousand foot and two hundred and seventy thousand horse; front to rear they stretched a thousand li, banners and drums in sight of one another.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十四 苻堅載記下
passages.textZh: 聞風聲鶴唳，皆謂晉師之至。
passages.textEn: [The fleeing troops,] hearing the wind and the cry of cranes, all took it for the Jin army coming.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.textZh: 玄先遣廣陵相劉牢之五千人直指洛澗，即斬梁成及成弟雲，步騎崩潰，爭赴淮水。
passages.textEn: Xie Xuan first sent Liu Laozhi, Chancellor of Guangling, straight at Luojian with five thousand men; he cut down Liang Cheng and his brother Yun at once, and their foot and horse broke and fled, scrambling for the Huai.

question.en: How large were the two armies?

claim.zh: 前秦：步卒六十餘萬、騎二十七萬，前鋒步騎二十五萬。
claim.en: Qin: over 600,000 foot and 270,000 horse, with a vanguard of 250,000.

accounts.quoteZh: 堅發長安，戎卒六十餘萬，騎二十七萬

claim.zh: 東晉：謝玄等所部共八萬。
claim.en: Jin: Xie Xuan and the other commanders had 80,000 in all.

accounts.quoteZh: 與叔父征虜將軍石、從弟輔國將軍琰、西中郎將桓伊、龍驤將軍檀玄、建威將軍戴熙、揚武將軍陶隱等距之，眾凡八萬。

claim.zh: 今人多認為前秦總數有誇大，實際投入淝水一線的是前鋒部隊。
claim.en: Modern historians mostly think the Qin total is exaggerated, and that only the vanguard was engaged on the Fei.

note.zh: 兩數同出唐修《晉書》，且晉、秦雙方史料都有誇大對方的動機。
note.en: Both figures come from the Tang-compiled Book of Jin, and both sides' records had reason to inflate the enemy.

fiction.zh: 「草木皆兵」一語源出《晉書·苻堅載記》（「北望八公山上草木，皆類人形」），屬史書敘事中的形容，不宜視為實錄。
fiction.en: The phrase "every tree and blade of grass a soldier" goes back to the Book of Jin's account of Fu Jian ("looking north, the plants on Mount Bagong all looked like men") — narrative colouring rather than record.

summary.zh: 義熙十二年，劉裕乘後秦姚興新死、諸子相爭，率軍北伐。次年檀道濟等進抵潼關，王鎮惡率水軍自黃河入渭水，八月攻克長安，生擒姚泓，後秦亡。劉裕旋即東歸，長安翌年為夏所奪。
summary.en: In 416, with Yao Xing of Later Qin newly dead and his sons fighting, Liu Yu marched north. The next year Tan Daoji and others reached Tong Pass, and Wang Zhen'e took a fleet from the Yellow River up the Wei, took Chang'an in the eighth month and captured Yao Hong: Later Qin was finished. Liu Yu soon went back east, and Xia took Chang'an the following year.

label.en: Wang Zhen'e up the Wei by water

passages.textZh: 初公平齊，仍有定關、洛之意，值盧循侵逼，故其事不諧。荊、雍既平，方謀外略。會羌主姚興死，子泓立，兄弟相殺，關中擾亂，公乃戒嚴北討。
passages.textEn: When the Duke had pacified Qi he already meant to settle Guanzhong and Luoyang, but Lu Xun's attack interfered. Once Jing and Yong were quiet he turned to foreign plans. Just then the Qiang ruler Yao Xing died and his son Hong succeeded; the brothers killed one another and Guanzhong was in turmoil, so the Duke put the army on a war footing and marched north.

passages.textZh: 八月，扶風太守沈田子大破姚泓於藍田。王鎮惡剋長安，生擒泓。九月，公至長安。
passages.textEn: In the eighth month Shen Tianzi, Governor of Fufeng, routed Yao Hong at Lantian; Wang Zhen'e took Chang'an and captured Yao Hong alive. In the ninth month the Duke reached Chang'an.

summary.zh: 始光四年，北魏太武帝西伐夏國，六月攻克都城統萬，赫連昌出奔上邽。魏軍所獲牛馬珍寶甚眾。
summary.en: In 427 Emperor Taiwu of Wei marched west against Xia and in the sixth month took its capital Tongwan; Helian Chang fled to Shanggui. The Wei army took vast numbers of horses, cattle and treasure.

passages.textZh: 獲馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊數千萬。以昌宮人及生口、金銀、珍玩、布帛班賚將士各有差。
passages.textEn: They took over three hundred thousand horses and tens of millions of cattle and sheep. Helian Chang's palace women and captives, gold, silver, rarities and cloth were shared out among the officers and men by rank.

confidenceNote.zh: 「索虜」是南朝史書對北魏的蔑稱。
confidenceNote.en: "Braided barbarians" (suolu) was the southern histories' insulting name for the Northern Wei.

summary.zh: 元嘉七年三月，宋文帝遣到彥之北伐，水軍入黃河。七月魏軍棄碻磝、滑臺而走，宋收復河南四鎮；但十月洛陽（金墉）、十一月虎牢相繼失陷。次年檀道濟救滑臺不及，滑臺陷落，宋軍退回。
summary.en: In the third month of 430 Emperor Wen of Song sent Dao Yanzhi north with a fleet into the Yellow River. In the seventh month the Wei garrisons abandoned Qiao'ao and Huatai and Song recovered the four strongholds south of the river — but Luoyang (Jinyong) fell back to Wei in the tenth month and Hulao in the eleventh. The next year Tan Daoji could not relieve Huatai in time; it fell, and the Song army went home.

passages.textZh: 三月戊子，遣右將軍到彥之北伐，水軍入河。
passages.textEn: In the third month, on wuzi, the General of the Right Dao Yanzhi was sent north, his fleet entering the Yellow River.

passages.textZh: 秋七月戊子，索虜碻磝戍棄城走。……戊戌，索虜滑臺戍棄城走。
passages.textEn: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuzi, the garrison of the "braided barbarians" at Qiao'ao abandoned the city and fled. … On wuxu the garrison at Huatai abandoned the city and fled.

passages.textZh: 戊寅，金墉城為索虜所陷。 十一月癸未，虎牢城復為索虜所陷。
passages.textEn: On wuyin, Jinyong fell to the braided barbarians. In the eleventh month, on guiwei, Hulao fell to them again.

summary.zh: 太延五年，北魏太武帝西征北涼，八月至姑臧，九月沮渠牧犍面縛出降。北方自此為北魏統一，與南朝宋形成南北對峙。
summary.en: In 439 Emperor Taiwu marched against Northern Liang, reached Guzang in the eighth month, and in the ninth month Juqu Mujian came out with his hands bound. The north was now united under Wei, facing Song in the south.

passages.textZh: 丙申，車駕至姑臧，牧犍兄子祖踰城來降，乃分軍圍之。 九月丙戌，牧犍兄子萬年率麾下來降。是日，牧犍與左右文武五千人面縛軍門，帝解其縛，待以藩臣之禮。
passages.textEn: On bingshen the imperial carriage reached Guzang; Mujian's nephew Zu climbed over the wall and came over, and the army was divided to surround the city. In the ninth month, on bingxu, Mujian's nephew Wannian came over with his men. That day Mujian and five thousand of his officials and officers came to the camp gate with their hands bound; the Emperor untied them and treated him with the courtesy due to a vassal.

summary.zh: 元嘉二十七年宋北伐失利後，北魏太武帝大舉南下，十二月抵達長江北岸瓜步，伐葦造筏，聲言渡江；建康戒嚴。次年正月魏軍北撤，沿途攻盱眙不下。江淮之間殘破極甚。
summary.en: After the failure of Song's northern campaign of 450, Emperor Taiwu came south in force and in the twelfth month reached Guabu on the north bank of the Yangtze, cutting reeds for rafts and threatening to cross; Jiankang was put under martial law. In the first month of 451 the Wei army withdrew, failing before Xuyi on the way. The land between the Huai and the Yangtze was devastated.

label.en: Prince of Yongchang via Shouyang to Liyang
Prince of Gaoliang from Shanyang to Guangling

passages.textZh: 燾至瓜步，壞民屋宇，及伐蒹葦，於滁口造箄筏，聲欲渡江。太祖大具水軍，為防禦之備。
passages.textEn: Tao reached Guabu, tore down people's houses and cut reeds, built rafts at the mouth of the Chu, and gave out that he would cross the river. Taizu assembled a great fleet and prepared the defence.

passages.textZh: 癸未，車駕臨江，起行宮於瓜步山。永昌王仁自歷陽至於江西，高涼王那自山陽至於廣陵，諸軍皆同日臨江，所過城邑，莫不望塵奔潰，其降者不可勝數。甲申，義隆使獻百牢，貢其方物，又請進女於皇孫以求和好。
passages.textEn: On guiwei the imperial carriage reached the Yangtze and a travelling palace was raised on Mount Guabu. Ren, Prince of Yongchang, came from Liyang to the river, and Na, Prince of Gaoliang, from Shanyang to Guangling; all the armies reached the river on the same day, and every town they passed fled at the sight of their dust; those who surrendered were past counting. On jiashen [Liu] Yilong sent a hundred sacrificial animals and local tribute, and asked to give a daughter in marriage to the imperial grandson to make peace.

passages.textZh: 庚午，虜偽主率大眾至瓜步。壬午，內外戒嚴。
passages.textEn: On gengwu the false ruler of the barbarians reached Guabu with his host. On renwu martial law was declared inside and outside the capital.

claim.zh: 宋文帝遣使獻禮，請以女嫁魏皇孫求和。
claim.en: Emperor Wen sent gifts and offered a daughter in marriage to make peace.

source.en: Book of Wei, Annals of Shizu

accounts.quoteZh: 甲申，義隆使獻百牢，貢其方物，又請進女於皇孫以求和好。

claim.zh: 宋書只記魏軍「聲欲渡江」與宋軍備水師防禦，其後魏軍「自瓜步退走」，不言宋求和。
claim.en: The Book of Song records only that Wei "gave out that it would cross" and that Song readied its fleet, then that Wei "withdrew from Guabu"; it says nothing of Song seeking peace.

source.en: Book of Song, Annals of Emperor Wen and the Suolu chapter

accounts.quoteZh: 丁亥，索虜自瓜步退走。

note.zh: 兩書各為本朝諱：魏書寫南朝示弱，宋書寫北軍自退。
note.en: Each history spares its own side: the Book of Wei has the south humbling itself, the Book of Song has the northern army simply leave.

summary.zh: 元嘉二十八年正月，北魏太武帝自瓜步北返，攻圍盱眙。守將臧質與太武帝往來書信相譏，堅守月餘；二月魏軍解圍而去。
summary.en: In the first month of 451, returning from Guabu, Emperor Taiwu laid siege to Xuyi. Its commander Zang Zhi traded insulting letters with him and held out for a month; in the second month the Wei army raised the siege and left.

passages.textZh: 燾與質書曰：「吾今所遣鬭兵，盡非我國人，城東北是丁零與胡，南是三秦氐、羌。設使丁零死者，正可減常山、趙郡賊；胡死，正減并州賊；氐、羌死，正減關中賊。卿若殺丁零、胡，無不利。」
passages.textEn: Tao wrote to Zang Zhi: "The fighting men I am sending now are none of them my own people. North-east of the city are Dingling and Hu; to the south, Di and Qiang of the Three Qin. If the Dingling die, that is just fewer bandits in Changshan and Zhao; if the Hu die, fewer bandits in Bing; if the Di and Qiang die, fewer bandits in Guanzhong. If you kill the Dingling and the Hu, I lose nothing."

passages.textZh: 質答書曰：「省示，具悉姦懷。爾自恃四脚，屢犯國疆，諸如此事，不可具說。王玄謨退於東，梁坦散於西，爾謂何以不聞童謠言邪：『虜馬飲江水，佛狸死卯年。』……
passages.textEn: Zang Zhi replied: "I have read your letter and see through your wicked heart. Trusting in your four legs, you have often violated our borders — more than can be told. Wang Xuanmo fell back in the east, Liang Tan scattered in the west — have you not heard the children's rhyme: 'When the barbarians' horses drink from the Yangtze, Foli will die in a mao year'?…"

passages.textZh: 丁酉，攻圍盱眙城。
passages.textEn: On dingyou [the Wei army] laid siege to Xuyi.

names.name: Loss of the lands north of the Huai

summary.zh: 宋明帝即位之初（466），諸王舉兵相爭，徐州刺史薛安都以彭城、司州刺史常珍奇以懸瓠降魏。宋軍反攻失敗，青州東陽、冀州歷城相繼陷落，至469年淮北青、冀、徐、兗四州盡歸北魏，南北邊界南移至淮河一線。
summary.en: When Emperor Ming of Song took the throne (466), princes rose against him; the governor of Xu, Xue Andu, surrendered Pengcheng to Wei, and the governor of Si, Chang Zhenqi, surrendered Xuanhu. Song's counter-attack failed; Dongyang in Qing and Licheng in Ji fell in turn, and by 469 all four provinces north of the Huai — Qing, Ji, Xu and Yan — were Wei's. The frontier moved south to the Huai.

passages.textZh: 九月，劉彧司州刺史常珍奇以懸瓠內屬。……劉彧徐州刺史薛安都以彭城內屬，彧將張永、沈攸之擊安都。
passages.textEn: In the ninth month, Chang Zhenqi, governor of Si Province for Liu Yu [Emperor Ming of Song], submitted with Xuanhu. … Xue Andu, Liu Yu's governor of Xu Province, submitted with Pengcheng; Yu's generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi attacked Andu.

passages.locator: 卷三十六 州郡志二 青州
passages.textZh: 明帝失淮北，於鬱洲僑立青州，立齊、北海、西海郡。
passages.textEn: When Emperor Ming lost the land north of the Huai, an émigré Qing Province was set up on Yuzhou island, with the commanderies of Qi, Beihai and Xihai.

names.name: Emperor Xiaowen moves the capital to Luoyang

summary.zh: 太和十七年，北魏孝文帝以南伐為名率軍自平城南下，九月至洛陽，群臣於馬前請停南伐，遂定遷都之計。十月幸金墉城、命李沖等營建洛京，告遷都於滑臺；次年十一月正式至洛陽，十二月改革衣服之制。
summary.en: In 493 Emperor Xiaowen led his army south from Pingcheng on the pretext of a campaign against the south. At Luoyang in the ninth month, his ministers begged before his horse to call it off, and the move of the capital was settled. In the tenth month he went to Jinyong and set Li Chong and others to building the new capital, and announced the move at Huatai; he arrived at Luoyang for good in the eleventh month of 494, and in the twelfth reformed the rules of dress.

passages.textZh: 丁丑，戎服執鞭，御馬而出，羣臣稽顙於馬前，請停南伐，帝乃止。仍定遷都之計。
passages.textEn: On dingchou, in armour and holding a whip, he rode out; the ministers knocked their heads on the ground before his horse and begged him to call off the southern campaign, and he stopped. So the plan to move the capital was settled.

passages.textZh: 冬十月戊寅朔，幸金墉城。詔徵司空穆亮與尚書李沖、將作大匠董爵經始洛京。
passages.textEn: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day, wuyin, he went to Jinyong and summoned the Minister of Works Mu Liang, the Secretary Li Chong and the Chief Architect Dong Jue to lay out the capital at Luoyang.

passages.textZh: 己丑，車駕至洛陽。
passages.textEn: On jichou the imperial carriage arrived at Luoyang.

passages.textZh: 壬寅，革衣服之制。
passages.textEn: On renyin the rules of dress were reformed.

summary.zh: 天監五年，北魏中山王元英率大軍圍鍾離，號稱百萬，於淮河上架橋連營。梁遣曹景宗、韋叡馳援，次年四月淮水暴漲，馮道根等乘戰艦焚斷魏軍浮橋，大破魏軍於邵陽洲，斬獲以萬計。
summary.en: In 506 Yuan Ying, Prince of Zhongshan, besieged Zhongli with an army said to number a million, bridging the Huai and linking his camps. Liang sent Cao Jingzong and Wei Rui to the relief; in the fourth month of 507, with the Huai in flood, Feng Daogen and others cut the Wei bridges with warships and the Wei army was routed at Shaoyang island, with tens of thousands killed or taken.

label.zh: 韋叡自合肥經陰陵大澤馳援
label.en: Wei Rui from Hefei through the Yinling marshes

passages.textZh: 叡曰：「鐘離今鑿穴而處，負戶而汲，車馳卒奔，猶恐其後，而況緩乎！魏人已墮吾腹中，卿曹勿憂也。」旬日而至邵陽。
passages.textEn: Wei Rui said: "Zhongli is living in holes it has dug, fetching water under shields made of doors. Even racing our carts and running our men we may be too late — how can we go slowly? The Wei army has already fallen into our belly; do not worry, gentlemen." In ten days he reached Shaoyang.

passages.textZh: 及淮水長，道根乘戰艦，攻斷魏連橋數百丈，魏軍敗績。
passages.textEn: When the Huai rose, Daogen took warships and cut several hundred zhang of the Wei bridges, and the Wei army was routed.

passages.textZh: 癸巳，曹景宗、韋叡等破魏軍於邵陽洲，斬獲萬計。
passages.textEn: On guisi, Cao Jingzong, Wei Rui and others routed the Wei army at Shaoyang island, killing or capturing tens of thousands.

question.en: Was the Wei army really a million strong?

claim.zh: 梁書稱魏軍「衆號百萬，連城四十餘」。
claim.en: The Book of Liang says the Wei army was "said to be a million, with over forty linked forts".

accounts.quoteZh: 衆號百萬，連城四十餘。

claim.zh: 「號」是號稱；實數不詳，今人估計遠少於此。
claim.en: "Said to be" — the real number is unknown and modern estimates are far lower.

confidenceNote.zh: 築堰之年見《梁書·武帝紀》；潰決的時間與死亡人數本圖尚未核對原文。
confidenceNote.en: The year of building is in the Book of Liang; the date of the collapse and the death toll have not yet been checked against the text.

summary.zh: 梁武帝為水淹北魏所據的壽陽，於天監十三年（514）在淮河浮山築堰，役使軍民甚眾，堰成後淮水倒灌。一般記載堰於516年秋淮水暴漲時潰決，沿淮死者十餘萬口。
summary.en: To flood Wei-held Shouyang, Emperor Wu of Liang began a dam across the Huai at Fushan in 514, using vast numbers of soldiers and labourers; once finished it backed the Huai up. The usual account is that it burst when the Huai flooded in the autumn of 516, drowning over a hundred thousand people along the river.

passages.textZh: 是歲作浮山堰。
passages.textEn: This year the Fushan dam was built.

confidenceNote.zh: 起事於沃野鎮，波及六鎮及河北、關隴；標記在沃野。
confidenceNote.en: It began at Woye and spread through the six garrisons, Hebei and Guanlong; the marker is at Woye.

summary.zh: 正光五年三月，沃野鎮人破落汗拔陵聚眾反，殺鎮將，北邊六鎮相繼響應。北魏遷洛後邊鎮軍人地位低落，積怨爆發。亂事延燒十餘年，爾朱榮、高歡、宇文泰皆由此崛起，北魏終於分裂。
summary.en: In the third month of 524 Poluohan Baling of the Woye garrison raised a following, killed the garrison commander and rebelled, and the other northern garrisons followed. Since the move to Luoyang the frontier soldiers had sunk in status, and their resentment exploded. The fighting spread for over a decade; Erzhu Rong, Gao Huan and Yuwen Tai all rose out of it, and Wei finally split.

passages.textZh: 三月，沃野鎮人破落汗拔陵聚眾反，殺鎮將，號真王元年。
passages.textEn: In the third month, Poluohan Baling of the Woye garrison raised a following and rebelled, killed the garrison commander, and proclaimed the first year of the True King.

confidenceNote.zh: 遇害人數諸書不一，本圖不取確數。
confidenceNote.en: The sources disagree on the number killed; no figure is given here.

summary.zh: 武泰元年，孝明帝暴崩，胡太后立幼主。爾朱榮以問罪為名自晉陽南下，立長樂王元子攸（孝莊帝），四月於河陰將胡太后與幼主沉入黃河，又召集王公百官加以屠戮。北魏朝廷精英幾被一網打盡。
summary.en: In 528 Emperor Xiaoming died suddenly and Empress Dowager Hu put an infant on the throne. Erzhu Rong came south from Jinyang to call her to account, set up Yuan Ziyou, Prince of Changle (Emperor Xiaozhuang), and in the fourth month at Heyin had the empress dowager and the infant drowned in the Yellow River and the assembled princes and officials slaughtered. The Wei court elite was all but wiped out.

passages.textZh: 壬寅，太原王尒朱榮上表，請追諡無上王為皇帝。餘死於河陰者，諸王、刺史贈三司，三品者令僕，五品者刺史，七品以下及民郡、鎮。
passages.textEn: On renyin Erzhu Rong, Prince of Taiyuan, petitioned that the Unsurpassed Prince be posthumously named emperor. Of the others who died at Heyin, princes and provincial governors were posthumously given the rank of the Three Excellencies; those of the third rank, Director or Vice-Director of the Secretariat; those of the fifth rank, governors; those of the seventh rank and below, and commoners, commandery or garrison posts.

summary.zh: 大通二年冬，梁武帝立北魏降王元顥為魏主，遣陳慶之率軍數千護送北還。次年陳慶之白袍軍自銍縣出發，轉戰至洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰。元顥入洛後不久為爾朱榮所敗，陳慶之全軍覆沒，僅以身免。
summary.en: In the winter of 528 Emperor Wu of Liang proclaimed the Wei prince Yuan Hao ruler of Wei and sent Chen Qingzhi with a few thousand men to escort him home. The next year the white-robed army set out from Zhi county and fought its way to Luoyang: thirty-two cities in a hundred and forty days, in forty-seven battles. Soon after Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he was beaten by Erzhu Rong; Chen Qingzhi's army was destroyed and he barely escaped.

passages.locator: 卷三十二 陳慶之傳
passages.textZh: 慶之麾下悉著白袍，所向披靡。先是洛陽童謠曰：「名師大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍。」自發銍縣至於洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。
passages.textEn: Qingzhi's men all wore white robes, and everything gave way before them. Before this a children's rhyme in Luoyang went: "Famous generals and great commanders, do not trust your walls — a thousand troops and ten thousand horse make way for the White Robes." From leaving Zhi county to reaching Luoyang, in fourteen ten-day periods they took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles, and nothing stood in their way.

question.en: Can Chen Qingzhi's record be trusted?

claim.zh: 梁書：十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。
claim.en: Book of Liang: thirty-two cities in a hundred and forty days, forty-seven battles, unstoppable.

accounts.quoteZh: 十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。

claim.zh: 當時北魏陷於內亂，元顥軍沿途多有降附；數字出自梁方史書，北方史料記述較簡略。
claim.en: Wei was in civil war and many places simply went over to Yuan Hao; the figures come from the Liang side, and the northern sources say much less.

confidenceNote.zh: 《魏書》成於北齊，稱孝武帝「為椿等迫脅」而西奔，立場偏於高氏。
confidenceNote.en: The Book of Wei was written under Northern Qi and says the emperor was "coerced" into fleeing west — the Gao family's point of view.

summary.zh: 永熙三年七月，北魏孝武帝與高歡決裂，西奔長安投宇文泰。高歡另立孝靜帝，十月遷都鄴，是為東魏；孝武帝旋為宇文泰所殺，宇文泰次年立文帝於長安，是為西魏。北方一分為二。
summary.en: In the seventh month of 534 Emperor Xiaowu of Wei broke with Gao Huan and fled west to Yuwen Tai at Chang'an. Gao Huan set up Emperor Xiaojing and in the tenth month moved the court to Ye — the Eastern Wei. Yuwen Tai soon killed Xiaowu and the next year set up Emperor Wen at Chang'an — the Western Wei. The north was split in two.

passages.textZh: 丁未，帝為椿等迫脅，遂出於長安。己酉，齊獻武王入洛，賀拔勝走還荊州。
passages.textEn: On dingwei, the Emperor, coerced by [Husi] Chun and others, left for Chang'an. On jiyou the Prince Xianwu of Qi entered Luoyang, and Heba Sheng fled back to Jing Province.

passages.textZh: 丙子，車駕北遷于鄴。詔齊獻武王留後部分。改司州為洛州
passages.textEn: On bingzi the imperial carriage moved north to Ye. The Prince Xianwu of Qi was ordered to stay behind and arrange matters. Si Province was renamed Luo Province

summary.zh: 大統三年十月，高歡率大軍西攻，宇文泰兵少，採李弼之策，據渭曲背水列陣，伏兵於蘆葦中，大破東魏軍。西魏乘勝取河東。
summary.en: In the tenth month of 537 Gao Huan attacked west with a large army. Yuwen Tai, with far fewer men, took Li Bi's advice, drew up in the bend of the Wei with his back to the river and hid troops in the reeds, and routed the Eastern Wei army. Western Wei went on to take Hedong.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.textZh: 冬十月壬辰，至沙苑，距齊神武軍六十餘里。齊神武聞太祖至，引軍來會。癸巳旦，候騎告齊神武軍且至。太祖召諸將謀之。李弼曰：「彼眾我寡，不可平地置陣。此東十里有渭曲，可先據以待之。」
passages.textEn: In winter, the tenth month, on renchen, he reached Shayuan, sixty li from the army of Shenwu of Qi [Gao Huan]. Hearing that Taizu had come, Shenwu brought his army to meet him. At dawn on guisi the scouts reported Shenwu's army near. Taizu called his generals to council. Li Bi said: "They are many and we are few; we cannot draw up on open ground. Ten li east of here is the bend of the Wei — let us take it first and wait for them."

summary.zh: 武定元年（大統九年）二月，東魏北豫州刺史高仲密以虎牢降西魏，宇文泰出兵接應。三月兩軍會戰於洛陽北邙山。西魏晨襲幾乎擒獲高歡，但終為東魏所敗，虎牢復歸東魏。
summary.en: In the second month of 543 Gao Zhongmi, Eastern Wei governor of North Yu, surrendered Hulao to Western Wei, and Yuwen Tai came to meet him. In the third month the armies met on Mount Mang north of Luoyang. A Western Wei dawn attack nearly captured Gao Huan, but in the end Eastern Wei won and Hulao went back to it.

passages.textZh: 三月壬辰，周文率衆援高慎，圍河橋南城。戊申，神武大敗之於芒山，擒西魏督將已下四百餘人，俘斬六萬計。
passages.textEn: In the third month, on renchen, Zhouwen [Yuwen Tai] came with his host to support Gao Shen and besieged the southern fort of the river bridge. On wushen Shenwu [Gao Huan] routed him at Mount Mang, capturing over four hundred commanders and officers and killing or taking some sixty thousand.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.textZh: 太祖留輜重於𤄊曲，士皆銜枚，夜登邙山。未明，擊之，齊神武單騎為賀拔勝所逐，僅而獲免。太祖率右軍若干惠等大破齊神武軍，悉虜其步卒。趙貴等五將軍居左，戰不利。齊神武軍復合，太祖又不利
passages.textEn: Taizu left his baggage at the bend of the Chan; with gags in their mouths his men climbed Mount Mang by night and attacked before dawn. Shenwu of Qi, alone on his horse, was chased by Heba Sheng and barely escaped. Taizu with the right wing under Ruogan Hui and others routed Shenwu's army and took all its foot soldiers. Zhao Gui and four other generals on the left fared badly. Shenwu's army re-formed, and Taizu again fared badly

question.en: How did the battle of Mangshan go?

claim.zh: 東魏大勝：擒西魏督將四百餘人，俘斬六萬。
claim.en: A great Eastern Wei victory: over 400 Western Wei officers captured, 60,000 killed or taken.

source.en: Book of Northern Qi, Annals of Shenwu

accounts.quoteZh: 神武大敗之於芒山，擒西魏督將已下四百餘人，俘斬六萬計。

claim.zh: 周書：西魏拂曉突襲，高歡單騎被追、僅以身免，西魏右軍大破東魏；但左軍失利，東魏重整後西魏再敗。
claim.en: Book of Zhou: a Western Wei dawn attack; Gao Huan, chased alone, barely escaped and the Western Wei right routed his army — but the left failed, the Eastern Wei army re-formed, and Western Wei lost again.

source.en: Book of Zhou, Annals of Emperor Wen

accounts.quoteZh: 未明，擊之，齊神武單騎為賀拔勝所逐，僅而獲免。

note.zh: 兩書詳略不同：北齊書只記東魏大勝，不言高歡險被擒；周書詳記晨襲，對失利一筆帶過。
note.en: Each history dwells on its own side's best moment: the Qi history gives only the Eastern Wei victory and omits Gao Huan's narrow escape; the Zhou history details the dawn attack and passes quickly over the defeat.

summary.zh: 武定四年九月，高歡傾力圍攻西魏玉壁，守將韋孝寬堅守。東魏堆土山、鑿地道、移汾水斷其水源，攻城五十日不下，死者七萬人。高歡憂憤成疾，次年病逝。
summary.en: In the ninth month of 546 Gao Huan threw everything at the Western Wei fort of Yubi, held by Wei Xiaokuan. Eastern Wei raised earth ramps, dug tunnels and diverted the Fen to cut off its water, but fifty days of assault failed and seventy thousand died. Gao Huan fell ill with grief and died the next year.

passages.textZh: 九月，神武圍玉壁以挑西師，不敢應。西魏晉州刺史韋孝寬守玉壁，城中出鐵面，神武使元盜射之，每中其目。
passages.textEn: In the ninth month Shenwu besieged Yubi to provoke the western army, which dared not answer. The Western Wei governor of Jin Province, Wei Xiaokuan, held Yubi; men in iron masks came out of the city, and Shenwu had Yuan Dao shoot at them, hitting them in the eye every time.

passages.textZh: 孝寬奪據土山，頓軍五旬，城不拔，死者七萬人，聚為一冢。
passages.textEn: Xiaokuan seized the earth ramp. The army sat before the city fifty days without taking it; seventy thousand died and were buried in a single mound.

fiction.zh: 高歡病中令斛律金唱《敕勒歌》、自和之的故事流傳甚廣，本條未錄原文核對。
fiction.en: The famous story that the sick Gao Huan had Hulü Jin sing the "Song of the Chile" and joined in is widely told; it has not been checked against the text here.

summary.zh: 太清二年八月，降梁的侯景自壽陽起兵，十月渡江圍建康臺城。圍城中引玄武湖水灌城，城中軍民死亡殆盡；次年三月臺城陷，梁武帝憂憤而死。侯景殘破江南，551年自立為帝，552年為王僧辯、陳霸先所敗被殺。
summary.en: In the eighth month of 548 Hou Jing, who had gone over to Liang, rose at Shouyang and in the tenth month crossed the Yangtze to besiege the palace city of Jiankang. Water from the Xuanwu lake was let into the city, and most of those inside died; in the third month of 549 the palace city fell and Emperor Wu died in grief and anger. Hou Jing laid waste the south, made himself emperor in 551, and was beaten and killed by Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian in 552.

passages.textZh: 材官將軍宋嶷降賊，因爲立計，引玄武湖水灌臺城，城外水起數尺，闕前御街並爲洪波矣。又燒南岸民居營寺，莫不咸盡。
passages.textEn: The engineer-general Song Ni went over to the rebels and showed them how to let the Xuanwu lake into the palace city; outside the walls the water rose several feet and the imperial avenue before the gate was a flood. They also burned the houses, barracks and monasteries on the south bank; nothing was left.

passages.textZh: 己酉，高祖以所求不供，憂憤寢疾。……五月丙辰，高祖崩于淨居殿，時年八十六。
passages.textEn: On jiyou Gaozu, his needs unmet, fell ill with grief and anger. … In the fifth month, on bingchen, Gaozu died in the Jingju Hall, aged eighty-six.

confidenceNote.zh: 焚書與被擄人數為通行記載，本條未錄原文核對。
confidenceNote.en: The burning of the library and the numbers taken are the usual account and have not been checked against the text here.

summary.zh: 承聖三年，西魏遣于謹等率軍攻梁元帝於江陵，城破，元帝被殺，王公百姓數萬口被擄往長安，元帝焚毀所藏圖書。西魏立蕭詧為梁主於江陵，史稱後梁。
summary.en: In 554 Western Wei sent Yu Jin and others against Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jiangling. The city fell, the emperor was killed, and tens of thousands of officials and commoners were carried off to Chang'an; the emperor burned his library before the end. Western Wei set up Xiao Cha as ruler of Liang at Jiangling — the "Later Liang".

confidenceNote.zh: 「景戌」即丙戌，唐人避諱改「丙」為「景」。
confidenceNote.en: The text writes jing for bing — a Tang-era taboo substitution.

summary.zh: 太建五年，陳宣帝遣吳明徹北伐北齊，七月克壽陽外城，八月山陽、盱眙等城相繼降，收復淮南。578年吳明徹進攻彭城，在呂梁為北周所擒，次年陳盡失淮南。
summary.en: In 573 Emperor Xuan of Chen sent Wu Mingche north against Northern Qi. In the seventh month he took the outer city of Shouyang, and in the eighth Shanyang, Xuyi and other towns surrendered: the land between the Huai and the Yangtze was won back. In 578 Wu Mingche, attacking Pengcheng, was captured by Northern Zhou at Lüliang, and the next year Chen lost all of Huainan again.

passages.textZh: 己巳，吳明徹軍次峽口，克其北岸城，南岸守者棄城走。周炅克巴州城。淮北絳城及穀陽士民，並誅其渠帥，以城降。景戌，吳明徹克壽陽外城。 八月乙未，山陽城降。壬寅，盱眙城降。
passages.textEn: On jisi Wu Mingche's army reached Xiakou [on the Huai], took the fort on the north bank, and the defenders of the south bank abandoned theirs and fled. Zhou Jiong took Bazhou. The people of Jiangcheng and Guyang north of the Huai killed their leaders and surrendered their towns. On bingxu Wu Mingche took the outer city of Shouyang. In the eighth month, on yiwei, Shanyang surrendered; on renyin, Xuyi.

summary.zh: 建德五年，周武帝東伐北齊，先克平陽，再破晉陽；次年正月甲午攻入鄴城，北齊後主出逃被擒。北方重歸統一。
summary.en: In 576 Emperor Wu of Zhou attacked Northern Qi, took Pingyang and then Jinyang; on jiawu in the first month of 577 he entered Ye, and the last Qi ruler fled and was caught. The north was one again.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.textZh: 甲午，帝入鄴城。齊任城王湝先在冀州，齊主至河，遣其侍中斛律孝卿送傳國璽禪位於湝。
passages.textEn: On jiawu the Emperor entered Ye. The Qi Prince of Rencheng, Jie, was in Ji Province; the Qi ruler, reaching the Yellow River, sent his attendant Hulü Xiaoqing with the seal of state to abdicate in Jie's favour.

summary.zh: 開皇八年冬，隋以晉王楊廣節度諸軍，總管九十、兵五十一萬八千，東至海、西至巴蜀，同時伐陳。次年正月賀若弼自廣陵渡江取京口，韓擒虎自橫江渡采石，入建康，俘陳後主，陳亡。南北分裂近三百年，至此復歸統一。
summary.en: In the winter of 588 Sui sent its armies against Chen under the command of Yang Guang, Prince of Jin: ninety commanders and 518,000 men, from the sea to Sichuan. In the first month of 589 He'ruo Bi crossed from Guangling and took Jingkou, Han Qinhu crossed from Hengjiang to Caishi and entered Jiankang, and the last ruler of Chen was captured. After nearly three hundred years of division the empire was whole again.

label.en: He'ruo Bi crosses from Guangling to Jingkou
Han Qinhu crosses from Hengjiang to Caishi
He'ruo Bi beats the Chen army at Mount Jiang

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.textZh: 辛未，賀若弼拔陳京口，韓擒虎拔陳南豫州。癸酉，以尚書右僕射虞慶則為右衞大將軍。丙子，賀若弼敗陳師於蔣山，獲其將蕭摩訶。韓擒虎進師入建鄴，獲其將任蠻奴，獲陳主叔寶。陳國平，合州三十，郡一百，縣四百。
passages.textEn: On xinwei He'ruo Bi took Jingkou from Chen and Han Qinhu took South Yu Province. On guiyou Yu Qingze was made Grand General. On bingzi He'ruo Bi beat the Chen army at Mount Jiang and took its general Xiao Mohe. Han Qinhu advanced into Jianye, took its general Ren Manu, and took the Chen ruler Shubao. Chen was pacified: thirty provinces, a hundred commanderies, four hundred counties.

passages.textZh: 三年春正月乙丑朔，霧氣四塞。是日，隋總管賀若弼自北道廣陵濟京口，總管韓擒虎趨橫江，濟採石，自南道將會弼軍。
passages.textEn: In the third year [589], spring, the first month, on the first day, yichou, fog covered everything. That day the Sui commander He'ruo Bi crossed from Guangling by the northern route to Jingkou, and the commander Han Qinhu made for Hengjiang and crossed at Caishi, to join Bi by the southern route.
